title: Aerodrome manual
text:
(a) The Aerodrome Operator  shall establish  and maintain an aerodrome manual, which is a
fundamental requirement for Aerodrome Certification and Landing Area Acceptance, that is
acceptable to the GCAA.
(b) The content of the aerodrome manual shall reflect the applicable elements and the requirements
set out in this CAR, and shall not contravene the scope of the Aerodrome Certificate or Landing
Area Acceptance. The aerodrome manual shall contain or refer to all necessary information for
the safe use, operation and maintenance of the aerodrome, its equipment, as well as its obstacle
limitation requiremetns  and protection surfaces and other areas associated with the aerodrome.
(c) The Aerodrome Operator  shall ensure that all aerodrome personnel and all other relevant
organisation’s personnel have easy access to the portions of the aerodrome manual that are
relevant to their duties and responsibilities.
(d) The Aerodrome Operator  shall:
(1) provide the GCAA with complete and current copy of the aerodrome manual ,
electronically;
(2) provide the GCAA with the intended amendments and revisions of the aerodrome
manual, for items requiring prior approval in accordance with ADR.OR.H.065 - Changes, in
advance of the effective date and ensure that they do not become effective before
obtaining the GCAA’s approval.
(e) The Aerodrome Operator  shall:
(1) review the content of the aerodrome manual at appropriate intervels, or  when changes
to the manual  is carried out, or upon request from the GCAA, in any case the periodic review
of the AD manual by AD operator shall not exceed a period of 24 months and ensure that
it is kept up to date and amended whenever necessary;
(2) make all aerodrome personnel and other relevant organisations aware of the changes
that are relevant to their duties and responsibilities.

(f) The Aerodrome Operator  shall ensure that any information taken from other approved
documents, and any amendment thereof, is correctly reflected in the aerodrome manual.
(g) The Aerodrome Operator  shall ensure that the aerodrome manual:
(1) is signed by the Accountable Manager of the aerodrome;
(2) is printed or is in electronic format and is easy to revise;
(3) has a system for version control management which is applied and made visible in the
aerodrome manual;
(4) observes human factors principles and is organised in a  manner that facilitates its
preparation, use and review; and
(5) be supported by a completed aerodrome manual checklist that is provided by the GCAA.
(h) The parts of the aerodrome manual shall be as follows:
(1) Part A- General;
(2) Part B- Aerodrome management system, qualification and training requirements;
(3) Part C- Particulars of the aerodrome site;
(4) Part D - Particulars of the aerodrome required to be reported to the Aeronautical
Information Service; and
(5) Part E- Particulars of the operating procedures of the aerodrome, its equipment and
safety measures.

title: Aerodrome manual
text:
GENERAL
(a) The aerodrome manual may vary in detail according to the complexity of the operation, and the
type of the aerodrome.
(b) The aerodrome manual or parts of it may be presented in any form, including electronic form. In
all cases, the accessibility, usability, and reliability should be assured.
(c) The aerodrome manual should be such that:

(1) all parts of the manual are consistent and compatible in form and content;
(2) the manual can be readily amended; and
(3) the content and amendment status of the manual is controlled and clearly indicated.
(d) The aerodrome manual should include a description of its amendment and revision process
specifying:
(1) the person(s) who may approve amendments or revisions;
(2) the conditions  for temporary  revisions and/or immediate  amendments , or revision
required in the interest of safety; and
(3) the methods by which all personnel and organisations are advised of changes to the
aerodrome manual.
(e) The aerodrome manual may contain parts of, or refer to other controlled documents, such as
aerodrome equipment manual, which are available at the aerodrome for use by the personnel.
(f) If a particular element is not included in an aerodrome manual because it is not applicable to the
aerodrome, the Aerodrome Operator  should state in the aerodrome manual:
(1) that the particular element is not applicable; and
(2) why the particular element is not applicable.

title: Aerodrome manual
text:
AERODROME MANUAL
(a) Form of the aerodrome manual
 The aerodrome manual is a key document both for the Aerodrome Operator  and the GCAA. The
manual is the source document describing how the aerodrome infrastructure, facilities, and
operational procedures, will operate safely.

 Apart from the operational procedures, the GCAA will expect the aerodrome manual to be an
accurate reflection of the day-to-day functioning of the aerodrome's SMS, and its safety culture.
It will need to show how the aerodrome intends to measure its performance against safety
targets and objectives. The reader of an aerodrome manual should be given a clear statement of
how safety is developed, managed, and maintained on the aerodrome. All safety policies,
operational procedures and instructions should be contained in detail when relevant or cross-
referenced to other controlled, formally accepted or recognised, publications.
 At larger aerodromes, the size and complexity of operations, and related procedures may
dictate that these procedures could not easily be included in a single document. In such
circumstances, it is acceptable to identify and reference within the aerodrome manual the
procedures which are not included within it. If this system is to be successful, it is essential that
any referenced information, documentation, and procedures are made available as necessary to
all operational staff in a similar way as the aerodrome manual itself. For that purpose, a
computerised database containing the referenced procedures and information could be suitable.
For many small aerodromes/LAA, the aerodrome manual can be both simple and brief as long
as it covers procedures essential for satisfactory day-to-day operations.
(b) Purpose of the aerodrome manual
 An efficient management structure and a systematic approach to aerodrome operation is
essential. The aerodrome manual should contain all the relevant information to satisfactorily
describe this structure. It is one of the means by which all relevant operating staff can be
informed as to their duties and responsibilities with regard to safety. It should describe the
aerodrome infrastructure, services and facilities, all operating procedures, and any restrictions on
aerodrome availability.

 Accountability for safety must start at the very top of any organisation. One of the key elements in
establishing safe working practices is the ‘top down’ approach where all staff should understand
the safety aims of the organisation, the chain of command, and their own responsibilities and
accountabilities. As safety management principles are applied, the aerodrome manual should
be expanded to describe clearly how the safety of operations is to be managed. To a reader or
user of the aerodrome manual, there should never be any doubt in terms of ‘safety accountability’
for each domain or activity described. Each section should define who is accountable, who is
responsible, who has the authority, who has the expertise, and who actually carries out the tasks
described in any section.
 The principle objective of an aerodrome manual should be to show how management will
accomplish its safety responsibilities. The aerodrome manual will set out the policy and expected
standards of performance, and the procedures by which they will be achieved.
 The Aerodrome Operator  should ensure that:
(1) the responsibilities of the Aerodrome Operator  are clearly described;
(2) the tasks and activities that are to be performed by the Aerodrome Operator  or third
party are listed; and
(3) the means and procedures in order to complete these tasks and activities are described or
appended, together with the necessary details on their frequencies and operating
modes.
 Where responsibilities are attributed to other stakeholders, the aerodrome manual should
clearly identify them.
(c) The aerodrome manual may be issued in separate parts.

title: Aerodrome manual
text:
AERODROME MANUAL - PARTS
The aerodrome manual should have the following structure, and include, at least, the following
information; if an item is not applicable, the indication ‘Not applicable’ or ‘Intentionally blank’ should be
inserted, along with the relevant reason:
(a) PART A- GENERAL

(1) Administration and control of the aerodrome manual including the following:
(i) Introduction
A. a statement signed by the Accountable Manager that the aerodrome manual is
prepared in accordance with the applicable requirements;
B. a statement signed by the Accountable Manager that the aerodrome manual
contains operational instructions that are to be complied with by the relevant
personnel;
C. a list and brief description of the various parts, their contents, applicability, and
use;
D. explanations, abbreviations, and definitions of terms needed for the use of the
manual;
(ii) System of amendment and revision
A. details of the person(s) responsible for the issuance and insertion of
amendments and revisions;
B. a record of amendments and revisions with insertion dates, and effective dates;
C. a description of the system for the annotation of pages, or paragraphs and their
effective dates;
D. a list of effective pages or paragraphs;
E. annotation of changes (in the text and, as far as practicable, on charts and
diagrams);
F. interim revisions;
G. description of the distribution system and a distribution list for the  aerodrome
manual, its amendments, and revisions.
(2) General information
 General information including the following:
(i) purpose and scope of the aerodrome manual;

(ii) legal requirements for an Aerodrome Certificate or Landing Area Acceptance and the
aerodrome manual as prescribed in these regulations;
(iii) conditions for use of the aerodrome by its users;
(iv) the obligations of the Aerodrome Operator ; rights of the GCAA and guidance to staff
on how to facilitate audits/inspections by GCAA personnel.
(b) PART B- AERODROME MANAGEMENT SYSTEM, QUALIFICATION AND TRAINING REQUIREMENTS
 A description of the management system, including the following:
(1) Aerodrome organisation and responsibilities including a description of the organisational
structure, including the general organogram and departments’ organograms. The
organogram should depict the relationship between the departments. Subordination and
reporting lines of all levels of organisational structure (Departments, Sections, etc.) related
to safety should be shown;
(2) Names, authorities, responsibilities, and duties of management of nominated postholders,
including their position and telephone numbers and matters for which they have
responsibility to deal directly with the GCAA on behalf of the organisation ; responsibi lities
and duties of other operational, maintenance personnel, as well of the aerodrome safety
committees and the Local Runway Safety Team and their functioning, should also be
included;
(3) A description of the Safety Management System, including:
(i) scope of the safety management system;
(ii) safety policy and objectives;
(iii) safety responsibilities of key safety personnel;
(iv) documentation control procedures;
(v) safety risk management process, including hazard identification and risk assessment
schemes;
(vi) monitoring of implementation and effectiveness of safety actions, and risk mitigation
measures;

(vii) safety performance monitoring;
(viii) safety reporting (including hazard reporting) and investigation;
(ix) emergency response planning;
(x) management of change (including organisational changes with regard to safety
responsibilities);
(xi) safety promotion; and
(xii) safety management system outputs.
(4) A description of the compliance monitoring and related procedures.
(5) A description of the quality management system for aeronautical data and aeronautical
information provision activities and related procedures, including those for meeting the
relevant safety, and security management objectives.
(6) Procedures for reporting to the GCAA including handling, notifying and reporting accidents,
serious incidents, and occurrences. This section should include, at least, the following:
(i) definition of accident, serious incident and occurrence and of the relevant
responsibilities of all persons involved;
(ii) illustrations of forms to be used (or copies of the forms themselves), instructions on
how they are to be completed, the addresses to which they should be sent and the
time allowed for this to be done;
(iii) procedures and arrangements for the preservation of evidence, including recordings,
following a reportable event;
(7) Procedures for:
(i) complying with safety decisions and publications;
(ii) reaction to safety issue; and
(iii) handling   of   safety   recommendations.
(8) A description of the method and procedures for recording aircraft movements, including
movement and aircraft type, dates, and number of passengers.

(9) Required aerodrome personnel qualifications. Moreover, procedures related to:
(i) the training programme, including the following:
A. responsibilities, frequencies, syllabi, duration of each type of training, method
for delivery of training and competency assessment, minimum performance to
be achieved by the trainees, and the identified training standards for all
personnel involved in th e operation, rescue and firefighting, maintenance and
management of the aerodrome, and those persons operating unescorted on the
movement area and other operational areas of the aerodrome.
B. procedures:
1) for training and competency assessment of the trainees;
2) to be applied in the event that personnel do not achieve the required
 standards.
(ii) the proficiency check programme, responsibilities and frequencies of proficiency
checks including:
A. checking methods and procedures;
B. procedures to be applied in the event that personnel do not achieve the
required standards;
C. the validation process to measure the effectiveness of the programme.
(10) Description of documentation to be stored and their storage periods.
(c) PART C- PARTICULARS OF THE AERODROME SITE
A description of the aerodrome site including in particular, the following information:
(1) a plan showing the distance of the aerodrome from the nearest city, town, or other populous
area;
(2) detailed maps and charts of the aerodrome showing the aerodrome’s location (longitude and
latitude) and boundaries, major facilities, aerodrome reference point, layout of runways,
taxiways and aprons, aerodrome visual and non-visual aids, and wind direction indicators;

(3) a plan showing the location of any aerodrome facilities and equipment outside the
boundaries of the aerodrome;
(4) description of the physical characteristics of the aerodrome, elevations, visual and non-visual
aids, as well as the information regarding the aerodrome reference temperature, strength of
pavements, rescue and firefighting level of protection, ground aids and main obstacles;
(5) description of equivalent level of safety if used and approved by the GCAA, special conditions,
and operating limitations; and all deviations from the regulatory provisions authorized by the
GCAA should be listed together with their validity and references to the related documents
(including any safety assessments);
(6) description of the types of operations that the aerodrome is approved to conduct including:
(i) a statement of the Aerodrome Reference Code, indicating the largest aircraft type
the aerodrome intends to serve; and type of traffic;
(ii) category of the runway(s) provided (non -instrument, instrument including non -
precision and precision);
(iii) the different runways and their associated level of service;
 Note.- Level of service is a description of the RVR for each runway.
(iv) the nature of aviation activities (commercial, passenger, air transport, cargo, aerial
work, general aviation etc.);
(v) the type of traffic permitted to use the aerodrome (international/national, IFR/VFR,
scheduled/non-scheduled);
(vi) the lowest meteorological conditions or RVR permitted for aircraft arrivals and
departures at the aerodrome;
(vii) any limitations on operations of the aerodrome, including area excluded from use by
commercial aircraft.
(d) PART D — PARTICULARS OF THE AERODROME REQUIRED TO BE REPORTED TO THE AERONAUTICAL
INFORMATION SERVICE

(1) The aeronautical information services available and the procedures for the promulgation of
general information, including the following:
(i) the name of the aerodrome;
(ii) the location of the aerodrome;
(iii) the geographical coordinates of the aerodrome reference point determined in
terms of the World Geodetic System — 1984 (WGS-84) reference datum;
(iv) the aerodrome elevation and geoid undulation;
(v) the elevation of each threshold and geoid undulation, the elevation of the runway
end, and any significant high and low points along the runway, and the highest
elevation of the touchdown zone of a precision approach runway;
(vi) the aerodrome reference temperature;
(vii) details of the aerodrome beacon; and
(viii) the name of the Aerodrome Operator  and contact details (including telephone
numbers) of the Aerodrome Operator  at which may be contacted at all times.
(2) Aerodrome dimensions and related information, inducing the following:
(i) Runway(s) — true bearing, designation number, length, width, displaced threshold
location( if any) , slope, surface type, type of runway and, for a precision approach
runway, the existence of an obstacle free zone;
(ii) length, width and surface type of strip, runway end safety areas, stopways; length,
width and surface type of taxiways; apron surface type and aircraft stand; clearway
length and ground profile;
(iii) declared distances;
(iv) visual aids for approach procedures, approach lighting type and visual approach
slope indicator system; marking and lighting of runways, taxiways, and aprons;
other visual guidance and control aids on taxiways and aprons, location and type of
visual docking guidance system; availability of standby power for lighting;

(v) the location and radio frequency of VOR aerodrome checkpoints;
(vi) the location and designation of standard taxi routes;
(vii) the geographical coordinates of each threshold, appropriate taxiway centre line
points, and aircraft stands; ( note.- If thresholds are displaced or the full runway length
is not availabe, the start and end coordinates are required to be reported);
(viii) the geographical coordinates, and the top elevation of significant obstacles in the
approach and take-off areas, in the circling area and in the surroundings of the
aerodrome (in the form of charts);
(ix) pavement surface type and bearing strength using the Aircraft Classification Rating
— Pavement Classification Rating (ACR-PCR) method;
(x) pre-flight altimeter check locations established and their elevation;
(xi) disabled aircraft removal plan, contact details (telephone/telex/fax numbers and e-
mail address) of the aerodrome coordinator for the removal of disabled aircraft,
and information on the capability to remove disabled aircraft, expressed in terms of
the largest aircraft type;
(xii) rescue and firefighting level of protection; types and amounts of extinguishing agents
normally available at the aerodrome; Nominate fire command call frequency as
121.6MHz; and
(xiii) Cases of equivalent level of safety, special conditions, and limitations.
(e) PART E — PARTICULARS OF OPERATING PROCEDURES OF THE AERODROME, ITS EQUIPMENT, AND
SAFETY MEASURES
 All procedures contained in the aerodrome manual should include and clearly define the roles,
responsibilities, and contact details of responsible aerodrome personnel, other persons or
organisations, including the third party organisations and other agencies involved, as appropriate,
and consider the need for establishing direct communication during non-working hours.
(1) Aerodrome reporting, including:

(i) arrangements and procedures for reporting changes to the aerodrome information
set out in the AIP and requesting the issue of NOTAM, including reporting changes to
the GCAA and recording of the reported changes;
(ii) procedures and frequencies for aeronautical data surveying, including areas to be
surveyed;
(iii) description of the procedures used for obtaining aeronautical data, ensuring it meets
quality standards, promulgation to the Aeronautical Information Service and review of
the published information.
(2) Procedures for accessing the aerodrome movement area, including:
(i) coordination with the security agencies;
(ii) prevention of unauthorised entry into the movement area.
(3) Procedures for the inspection, assessment and reporting of the condition of the aerodrome
movement area and other operational areas and facilities, (including runway surface friction
characteristics assessments and water-depth measurements), including:
(i) formal arrangements and means of communicating with the air traffic services unit
during inspections;
(ii) inspection checklists, logbook, and record-keeping; and
(iii) inspection intervals and times; reporting results and follow-up actions.
(4) Procedures for the inspection, routine and emergency maintenance of visual and non-
visual aids, as appropriate, and the aerodrome electrical systems, including:
(i) inspection checklists, logbook, and record keeping; and
(ii) inspection intervals and times; reporting results and follow-up actions.
(5) Operating, maintenance and repair instructions, servicing information, troubleshooting and
inspection procedures of aerodrome equipment.
(6) Procedures for:

(i) maintenance of the movement area, including paved and unpaved area, runways,
taxiways and their strips and aerodrome drainage;
(ii) friction testing, assessment and corrective programme for removal of rubber build
up or surface rehabilitation on the runway;
(iii) overload operations.
(7) Procedures for managing aerodrome works, including:
(i) coordinating, planning, and carrying out construction and maintenance work; and
(ii) arrangements and means of communicating with air traffic services unit and other
stake holders during the progress of such work.
(8) Procedures for apron management, including:
(i) point and procedure for transfer  of the aircraft between air traffic services unit, and
the apron management unit, where applicable;
(ii) allocation of aircraft parking positions;
(iii) engine start and aircraft push-back; and
(iv) marshalling and ‘follow-me’ service.
(9) Procedures for apron safety management, including:
(i) protection from jet blasts and downwash;
(ii) enforcement of safety precautions during aircraft refuelling operations;
(iii) FOD prevention, including apron cleaning/sweeping;
(iv) monitoring compliance of personnel on the apron with safety procedures; and
(v) escorting, controlling and protecting passengers on the apron, from vehicular
traffic and operating aircraft, use of predetermined routes, and avoiding
interference with stationary aircraft ground servicing activities.
(10) Procedures for airside vehicle control:

(i) procedures for the control and limitation of the number of vehicles operating on
the movement area, issuance of authorisations and temporary permits of vehicles
operating on or in the vicinity of the movement area, including driver’s obligations,
traffic rules, right of way, speed limits,  and procedures for issuing driving
authorisations and permits, and enforcement procedures;
(ii) procedures for escorting vehicles occasionally used in areas where radio and
transponder or equivalent is required, as well as for vehicles temporarily permitted
to operate on the movement area;
(iii) procedures and responsibilities for establishing and monitoring the implementation
of the maintenance programme for vehicles operating on the movement area and
other operating areas.
(11) Procedures for wildlife hazard management, including assessing wildlife hazards and
arrangements for implementation of the wildlife control programme, and promulgation of
the relevant information to the AIS.
(12) Procedures for:
(i) obstacle control and monitoring within and outside of the aerodrome boundaries,
and notification to the GCAA, of the nature and location of obstacles, and any
subsequent addition, or removal of obstacles for action as necessary, including
amendment of the AIS publications;
(ii) monitoring and mitigating hazards related to human activities and land-use, on the
aerodrome and its surroundings; and
(iii) maintenance of relevant inspection checklists, logbook, and record keeping;
inspection intervals and times; reporting results and follow-up actions.
(13) Aerodrome emergency plan including:
(i) dealing with emergencies at the aerodrome or in its surroundings;
(ii) tests for aerodrome facilities and equipment to be used in emergencies, including
their frequency; and
(iii) exercises to test emergency plans, including their frequency.

(14) Rescue and firefighting, including description of facilities, equipment, personnel and
procedures for meeting the promulgated level of protection.
(15) Removal plan of disabled aircraft, including relevant formal arrangements, equipment,
and procedures for its implementation.
(16) Procedures used for the safe handling and storage of hazardous material on the aerodrome,
including the following:
(i) details of special areas on the aerodrome set-up for the storage of flammable liquids
(including aviation fuels) and any other hazardous material;
(ii) the method to be followed for the delivery, storage, dispensing and handling of
hazardous materials;
(iii) description of the system in place to test the quality of aviation fuel prior to
dispensing into aircraft; and
(iv) description of the procedures in place on the apron to ensure safety during aircraft
refuelling/defueling operations.
(17) Low visibility operations:
description of operational procedures, including coordination with air traffic services unit and
where applicable, apron management unit, standard taxiing routes, control of activities, and
measurement and reporting of runway visual range.
(18) Procedures for operations in adverse weather.
(19) Procedures for night operations.
(20) Procedures for the protection of radar and other navigational aids, control of activities, and
ground maintenance in the vicinity of these installations.
(21) Procedures for the operation of aircraft that exceeds the certified design character of the
aerodrome, including taxiing routes.
(22) Procedures and measures for the prevention of fire at the aerodrome.
(23) Communication procedures, including:

frequencies and phraseology to be used when communicating with the air traffic services;
vehicle call signs; communication signals to be used in case of radio communication
failure; communication via the air traffic services provider; and dissemination of significant
information.
(24) Aircraft towing procedures, including:
 designated routes to be used; lights to be displayed by aircraft; communication procedures;
guidance to be provided; measures for ensuring safety of towing operation in adverse weather
conditions, including visibility and weather phenomena in which towing is limited or not
permitted.
(25) Procedures for the handover of activities between aerodrome personnel, including
description of the system for the provision of operational information to other
organisations operating at the aerodrome;
(26) (Intentionally left blank).
(27) Procedure for managing changes.
(28) Method of calculating reduced declared distances when there are temporary objects
infringing the runway strip, or the approach and take-off surfaces or for other reasons when
the threshold has to be displaced.
(29) Procedures and responsibilities for handling of activities and / or services  that are fully
contracted to a third party including the focal point for the contracted organisation.

title: Aerodrome manual
Scope
text:
Unless otherwise specified, the requirements of this section are applicable to land and water aerodromes,
used for domestic and/or international flights.

title: Certification obligations
text:
Prior to commencing the operation of an aerodrome, the Aerodrome Operator  shall obtain the applicable
Aerodrome Certificate issued by the GCAA.

title: Expression of interest for certification of an aerodrome
text:
The applicant for an Aerodrome Certificate shall formally inform the GCAA  in writing of their interest to
develop and operate an aerodrome.

title: Expression of interest for certification of an aerodrome
text:
EXPRESSION OF INITIAL INTEREST
(a) The applicant for Aerodrome Certificate should arrange for a  meeting with the GCAA and provide
details of the proposed aerodrome site as well as concept of operations.
 The applicant should make arrangements for its key personnel to be present during this meeting.
During this meeting, the applicant should present to the GCAA their plans with regard to the
aerodrome design and operations.
(b) During the meeting, the applicant may be:
(1) provided by the GCAA with general information about the applicable requirements  for the
aerodrome certificate, such as need for Aerodrome Registration, ownership details and point
of contact, etc;
(2) provided with copies of the applicable requirements, and a description of the procedures
 that are followed during the certification process; and
(3) informed by the GCAA about possible approvals, permits, or clearances that may be
 needed to be obtained from other authorities.
(4) Informed by the GCAA about the subsequent steps including – application for Regulatory
Design Review and application for aerodrome certificate once the construction is completed.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
(a) Pursuant to the United Arab Emirates Federal Act No. 20 (1991) Promulgating The Civil Aviation Law
Article 27 and to the Civil Aviation Regulations (CARs) for the time being in force , an Aerodrome
Certificate may be granted  by the GCAA, if it is satisfied that an applicant is competent, having
regard to the applicant’s previous conduct and experience, the equipment, organisation, staffing,
maintenance and other arrangements, to ensure that the aerodrome and airspace are safe for use
by aircraft.
(b) The requirement for Aerodrome Certificate is as follows:
 Aerodromes that are:
(1) used for international flights; or
(2) used for domestic flights when used for air services (These aerodromes are characterised as
commercial facilities available to the general public for ticketed or charter operations for
domestic .) ; or
(3) using instrument approach or departure procedures.
These aerodromes are characterised as commercial facilities available to the general public for
ticketed or charter operations for domestic or international flights.
(c) The applicant for an Aerodrome Certificate shall be the operator of the aerodrome who can be:
(1) the owner of the land on which the aerodrome is located; or
(2) the occupier of the land on which the aerodrome is located; or
(3) the actual person or organisation operating the aerodrome and holding a formal consent
from the owner or occupier of the land on which the facility is located.
(d) The application for Aerodrome Certificate  shall include The Federal Cabinet approval for
international airports.
(e) The application for an Aerodrome Certificate and subsequent document submissions shall be made
in a form and manner established by the GCAA that includes no -objections certificates, approvals.
Applicant for Aerodrome Certificate shall obtain approvals from GCAA in relation to Airspace and
all relevant agencies, authorities and entities including those mentioned in AMC2 ADR.OR.C.010(e).

(f) The applicant shall pay the applicable fees.
(g) The applicant shall provide the GCAA with the following:
(1) declaration of compliance and the completed compliance register;
(2) elements that are non- compliant and the associated risk assessment;
(3) documentation demonstrating how it will comply with the applicable requirements. Such
documentation shall include a procedure, describing how changes will be managed and
notified to the GCAA; subsequent changes to these procedures shall require prior appro val
by the GCAA.
(h) Applicant for Aerodrome Certificate  shall demonstrate to the GCAA their compliance to the
requirements of CAR AGA PART ADR, their formal arrangements for safeguarding of area within the
OLS and beyond.
(i) The applicant shall satisfy the certification requirement at each stage of the application process as
detailed in the GM1 ADR.OR.C.010(i).
(j) The applicant for an Aerodrome Certificate shall apply and obtain a no objection to the regulatory
design review and shall  not commence any construction activity until they receive a no -objection
to the  regulatory design review.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
AERODROME CERTIFICATE APPLICATION PROCESSING STAGES
Table OR-C- 1:Application for Aerodrome Certification - processing stages
Stage 1  Expression of Interest • Aerodrome Registration (see ADR.OR.C.010(c)
Registration of the organisation.)
Stage 2 Regulatory Design Review
(Applicant to apply for
Regulatory Design Review)

the applicant with the aerodrome owner).

• Security Clearance, Air space (see AMC2
ADR.OR.C.010(e)- other no-objections, approvals,
agreements and permissions).

• Compliance Matrix based on the CS in CAR AGA
PART ADR.

Note: Applicant for an aerodrome certificate may choose to  commence the pre- requisites for application,

aerodromes), manual acceptance (see AMC1 ADR.OR.C.010(e)(g) Aerodrome manual, AEP, SMS)
etc, ahead of the stage 3.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
RELATIONSHIP OF THE APPLICANT WITH THE AERODROME OWNER
(a) The applicant should provide the GCAA with all information necessary to demonstrate to the GCAA
its relationship with the aerodrome owner, and/or the owner of the land to be used for the
aerodrome development.
(b) Such documentation should include, but is not limited to, relevant portions of  contracts, lease
agreements, authorisations between the persons involved, etc.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
REGISTRATION  OF THE ORGANISATION
(a) Applicant should register their organization in the GCAA’s website, in order to make their
application through GCAA’s e-services or through other means established for this purpose by the
GCAA.
(b) Applicants should provide  evidence of their identity such as establishment / trade license
documentation and official documents as required during the registration process.
(c) Applicant should provide all documents and information as required in the application portal.
(d) Applicants should have secure access to the GCAA e -Services, available on the GCAA’s website:
www.gcaa.gov.ae. Applicants who do not have access to the GCAA’s e-Services must make an initial
request through GCAA’s customer service channels.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
INFORMATION TO BE PROVIDED TO THE GCAA FOR REGULATORY DESIGN REVIEW
(a) The location of the aerodrome, and its boundaries, including maps and charts to indicate various
facilities and area in the aerodrome.
Maps should clearly indicate the aerodrome operational area which include, at least, runways,
taxiways, aprons, associated strips, runway end safety areas, stopways, clearways, aerodrome
visual aids, fixed aerodrome equipment, other aerodrome operational areas, areas adjacent to the
movement area. This defined area will be subject to safety oversight by the GCAA following the
issue of an Aerodrome Certificate, and should be subject to the Aerodrome Operator’s internal
compliance monitoring and safety management activities.

Aerodrome boundary should not be confused with the boundaries established for other purposes,
such as fences, the land ownership boundaries used by local planning authorities, or those used to
designate security restricted zones ,custom controlled areas, etc.
(b) The type of operations at the aerodrome including:
(1) the aircraft types to be served at the aerodrome, and the critical aircraft type to be used for
the design of the aerodrome;
(2) the type of approaches, landing, and/or take-off operations on each runway/FATO;
(3) operations during the day and/or night;
(4) operational concept and the associated airspace;
(5) any limitations to the operation of the aerodrome;
(6) the design and facilities of the aerodrome, in accordance with the applicable Certification
Specifications established by the GCAA;
(7) unmanned aircraft operations including fuelling and charging facilities.
(c) Information about the location of the aerodrome - the exact location of the aerodrome should be
depicted on a map of a suitable scale acceptable to the GCAA.
(d) Drawings in suitable scale , electronic format  acceptable to the GCAA should contain:
(1) orientation of Runway(s) / FATOs;
(2) the dimensions of the aerodrome’s physical characteristics;
(3) the visual and non-visual aids;
(4) the obstacle limitation surfaces, and any other surfaces applicable; and
(5) the aerodrome facilities, installations, and fixed equipment and their location.
(e) Description, height, and location of obstacles, in accordance with the applicable aeronautical data
requirements.
(f) The applicant should identify the applicable Certification Specifications for the design and type of
operations of the proposed aerodrome and provide the GCAA with evidence that the proposed
design and operation complies with applicable regulations , the a pplicant should also provide the
GCAA with:
(1) the compliance register in the form and manner as established by the GCAA;

(2) the Certification Specifications for which it proposes to show compliance in a different
manner and demonstrate an equivalent level of safety. Such a proposal has to be acceptable
to the GCAA. In such cases, the applicant should also propose the method tha t will be used
to demonstrate compliance and achieve an equivalent level of safety, and submit all
necessary documentation to support the proposal.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
OTHER NO-OBJECTIONS, APPROVALS, AGREEMENTS AND PERMISSIONS
(a) A letter of no objection should be obtained from the Appropriate Authorities ensuring that the
necessary formal arrangements have been made with regard to the protection of the Obstacle
Limitation Surfaces (OLS).
(b) Applicants should obtain required approvals from other Appropriate Authorities (i.e. municipalities,
local planning authorities, civil defense, local departments of civil aviation, etc.); Applicant should
also establish coordination with entities such as environmental agency, security agency  as
appropriate.
(c) In addition to the application for an Aerodrome Certificate, other certification or approvals should
be required if Air Navigation Services such as ATS, CNS, MET and AIS is to be provided.
(d) Applicants may be required to apply for other certificates or approvals from the GCAA; this will be
dependent upon the scale and type of operations the aerodrome is intended to be used. Other
areas that require certification or approval are:
(1) Air Navigation Services:
  For the purposes of arrangements for Air Navigation services.
(2) Airspace:
 For the purpose of ensuring the suitability of the proposed site from an airspace perspective,
taking into consideration the proximity of the aerodrome to other  aerodromes and landing
sites, including military aerodromes , obstacles and terrain , any excessive operational
restriction requirements, any existing restrictions such as – special use airspace,  controlled
airspace; and any existing flight procedures.
(3) Aviation Security:
(A) Security clearance to confirm that supporting resources and facilities required  by
aviation security services are made available at facilities serving civil aviation.

(B) Applicants should, prior to the issue of a Regulatory Design Review  and for aviation
activity, obtain a security clearance from GCAA through the established means.

(e) There may also be other bodies that the applicants should inform in their own interests and it is the
responsibility of the Aerodrome Operator  to obtain the appropriate approvals. The application for
planning/building permissions and the request for an Aerodrome Certificate  are not
interdependent and are required to be made separately.
(f) As a part of the aerodrome certification process, the physical characteristics and design should
consider, where appropriate, land-use and environmental control measures.
(g) Previously issued approvals, if any, will generally be reassessed each 12 months if there are delays
or extended periods of inactivity.
(h) Applicant should have formal arrangement (MOU or agreement) with the AIS to ensure up-to-date
information of aerodrome safety-related conditions are published.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
METEOROLOGICAL STUDY
The applicant should have details of the study of the area of the aerodrome, including temperature,
visibility, ceiling and wind conditions; moreover, the study should provide information on wind conditions
occurring with poor visibility and/or low cloud base at the aerodrome, and their frequency, as well as the
accompanying wind direction and speed.
For Meteorological requirements refer to CAR ANS- PART MET- AERONAUTICAL METEOROLOGY SERVICE
PROVIDERS.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
APPLICABLE FEES
Service Fees, as published on the GCAA’s website are varied from time to time and should be paid to the
GCAA:
(a) during the initial Aerodrome Certificate; and
(b) on a periodic basis after the grant of an Aerodrome Certificate;
for each aerodrome.
Note.- Payment of the GCAA’s service fee does not guarantee the grant or continuation for aerodrome
operations  or of an Aerodrome Certificate.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
AERODROME MANUAL, AERODROME EMERGENCY PLAN, SAFETY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
(a) The manuals mentioned below and their amendments should be submitted to the GCAA in
electronic format that allows the GCAA to review, store, and reproduce it.
(1) an electronic version of the Aerodrome Manual, as required by ADR.OR.B.005 - Aerodrome
Manual , including the Aerodrome Manual Checklist;
(2) an electronic version of the Aerodrome Operator ’s Safety Management System (SMS)
manual as required by CAR SMS ,including the SMS manual checklist;
(3) an electronic version of the Aerodrome Emergency Plan (AEP) as required by P ART ACM,
including an AEP manual checklist.
(b) The GCAA will evaluate and verify if :
(1) the Aerodrome Manual contains all pertinent information on the aerodrome site, facilities,
services, equipment, operating procedures, organization and management;
(2) the Aerodrome Operator’s Safety Management System and supporting operating procedures
make satisfactory provision for the safety of aircraft;
(3) the aerodrome Rescue Firefighting Service is staffed, trained, equipped, operated and
organised to the meet the applicable requirements.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
ADEQUACY OF STRUCTURE AND RESOURCES
(a) The applicant should provide all necessary information needed in order to demonstrate to the
GCAA that its proposed organisation and management are suitable, and properly matched to the
scale and scope of the operation.
(b) Evidence of adequacy of resources to operate the aerodrome in accordance with ADR.OR.A.025 -
Personnel requirements- Aerodrome Certificate, to  enable the GCAA to assess each nominated
aerodrome Post Holder based on the assessment criteria as established in this CAR.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
ASSESSMENTS AND  EVALUATIONS
(a) The GCAA’s assessments, site visits and inspections will assess inter -alia physical characteristics,
visual aids (markings, lights, signs and markers), obstacle environment.
(b) Before granting an Aerodrome Certificate, the GCAA will verify that:

(1) the aerodrome’s facilities, services ,equipment and systems are in accordance with the Civil
Aviation Regulations and further to review, inspection or Aerodrome Certificate verification
audit;
(2) the Aerodrome Operator ’s processes and procedures as referenced in the Aerodrome
Manual;
(3) the applicant’s ability to operate and maintain the aerodrome properly.
(c) The applicant should provide   , documentation to demonstrate how it will comply with the
applicable requirements of this CAR and any other applicable requirements.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
NON-COMPLIANCE
(a) The Aerodrome Operator, should identify and inform the GCAA of  all the applicable Certification
Specification that they are non -compliant with. Such information along with the associated risk
assessment should be provided to the GCAA.
(b) The Aerodrome Operator should also identify and inform the GCAA of all the applicable Certification
Specification elements that they are non -compliant and wish to propose an equivalent level of
safety  that demonstrates how they meet the intent of the CS.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
ISSUANCE OR REFUSAL OF AERODROME CERTIFICATE
(a) The GCAA will only issue an Aerodrome Certificate, when it is completely satisfied that all regulatory
and critical safety elements have been adequately addressed; this may require a further GCAA audit
/ inspection follow-up visit and / or special additional operating approvals. This includes evidence
of any prior approvals or permissions.
(b) The GCAA may impose operating restrictions and/or sanctions at an aerodrome.
(c) After completion of the processing of the application, the GCAA while granting the Aerodrome
Certificate, may endorse the conditions of the type of use of the aerodrome and other details as
shown in the Aerodrome Certificate.
(d) In the event of non -compliance with the requirements of this CAR or unresolved safety
deficiencies/concerns, the GCAA may refuse to grant an Aerodrome Certificate, in such cases, will
notify the applicant in writing of its reasons.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
TIMESCALE FOR PROCESSING OF APPLICATIONS
(a) Applicants should engage with the GCAA sufficiently early to allow completion of pre -certification
activities, including regulatory design review, acceptance of nominated Post Holders, acceptance
of the Aerodrome Manual, verification of infrastructure and any required operational, safety
management or security-related coordination.
(b) The GCAA’s service level for processing a formal Aerodrome Certificate application applies only
once the application is complete and the GCAA is satisfied that the applicable pre -requisites have
been submitted and accepted, or otherwise addressed to the satisfaction of the GCAA.
(c) The application processing timescale does not include time required by the applicant to design,
construct, modify, validate or rectify aerodrome infrastructure; develop or amend manuals;
nominate or replace Post Holders; implement the Safety Management Sys tem; close findings;
obtain no-objections or approvals from other authorities; or submit acceptable corrective action
plans.
(d) Where aerodrome infrastructure development or modification is required, such activity shall be
processed through the aerodrome infrastructure project process before, or in parallel with,
certification as determined by the GCAA.
(e) The formal application should be accompanied by the prescribed service fee, the Aerodrome
Certificate application form, the accepted Aerodrome Manual, evidence of accepted Post Holders,
evidence of infrastructure compliance or accepted deviations, and any other documentation
required by the GCAA.
(f) The GCAA may conduct a certification audit or inspection, including verification of aerodrome
operations and safety management implementation, before issuing the Aerodrome Certificate.
(g) The GCAA will issue the Aerodrome Certificate only when satisfied that the applicant has
demonstrated compliance with CAR AGA and that all regulatory and critical safety matters have
been adequately addressed.
(h) The GCAA cannot undertake to reach a certification decision within a particular timescale or to
meet a commercial deadline set by the applicant.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
PROMULGATION OF STATUS OF THE AERODROME CERTIFICATE
Upon:
(a) successful issuance of the Aerodrome Certificate; and

(b) the satisfactory submission of details for the AIP publication by the Aerodrome Operator , as
required by the relevant CAR.
The GCAA will promulgate the status of the certificate in the AIP.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
AERODROME CERTIFICATE
(Intentionally left blank)

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
GENERAL - AERODROME NAMING AND ALLOCATION OF ICAO CODE
(a) The naming of an aerodrome is directly connected with aeronautical communications and flight
safety information. It is therefore important that aerodrome is representative of its location (the
nearest city, town or village) and should not have the potential to be confused with another
aerodrome.
(b) Aerodrome operator should apply to the GCAA for assignment of four -letter ICAO code. The
decision to assign a code for the aerodrome and get it validated through ICAO will remain with the
GCAA and is subject to confirmation by ICAO.
(c) ICAO Document 7910 - Location Identifiers contains codes allocated by national governments on
behalf of ICAO, to airports, airfields and other facilities such as ATC and weather stations.

title: Application for an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
REGULATORY DESIGN REVIEW
(a) GCAA’s issuance of no-objection to the  Regulatory Design Review  is based on the assessment of
the information provided by the applicant and  is valid for a period of one year. If construction of
the aerodrome has not been commenced by that time, the applicant should request for an
extension of the Regulatory Design Review  to ensure that the proposal remains in compliance with
GCAA Regulations.
(b) The issue of a  no-objection by the GCAA for the Regulatory Design Review  does not permit the
aerodrome to be used for operations until when construction is completed and an Aerodrome
Certificate is applied for obtained from the GCAA.

title: Scope of the Aerodrome Certificate
text: An Aerodrome Operator  shall comply with the scope and conditions of the Aerodrome Certificate.

title: Continued validity of an Aerodrome Certificate
text:
(a) The GCAA may only grant and permit an Aerodrome Certificate to continue where it is satisfied that
the Aerodrome Operator  can ensure that the aerodrome and its airspace are safe for use by
aircraft.
(b) An Aerodrome Certificate shall remain valid subject to:
(1) the Aerodrome Operator  remaining in compliance with the relevant requirements of this
CAR, and other applicable regulations and the aerodrome remaining in compliance with their
compliance register;
(2) the satisfactory outcome of regulatory surveillance activities;
(3) the Aerodrome Operator’s handling of findings (as specified in ADR.OR.J.020 -Findings and
corrective actions), to the satisfaction of the GCAA;
(4) the GCAA being granted access to the Aerodrome Operator ’s organisation as defined in

-Granting of access, to  determine continued compliance with the relevant
requirements of this CAR;
(5) the aerodrome operations are conducted within the scope and conditions as detailed in the
Aerodrome Certificate;
(6) the Aerodrome Certificate not being suspended , surrendered or revoked;
(7) payment of all applicable service fees as published by the GCAA.
(c) The validity of the Aerodrome Certificate is based upon the physical characteristics, type of use of
the aerodrome and continued operation in accordance with the GCAA Publications.
(d) Any change made to the physical characteristics  as declared in the compliance register ,
aeronautical publications, use of the aerodrome, as documented in the aerodrome manual, that is
not accepted by the GCAA shall invalidate an Aerodrome Certificate.
(e) Upon revocation or surrender, the Aerodrome Certificate shall be returned to the GCAA without
delay.

title: Amendment to Aerodrome Certificate
text:
The Aerodrome operator shall submit the following with any request for amendment in certificate:
(a) detailed account of the proposed amendment including the reasons for the amendment;
(b) an assessment of the safety risks associated with any change in use or operation of the aerodrome
including, where appropriate, the findings of any aeronautical study undertaken on behalf of the
operator;
(c) particulars of any consequential changes to the AIP, aerodrome manual and aerodrome emergency
plan; and
(d) any other request as notified by the GCAA.

title: Amendment to Aerodrome Certificate
Restriction, suspension of revocation of Aerodrome Certificate
text:
(a) Federal Act 20 - Article 27 provides that the GCAA may, on sufficient safety grounds revoke or
suspend an Aerodrome Certificate.
(b) The Aerodrome Certificate shall be restricted, suspended or revoked by the GCAA , if in the view of
the GCAA, the safety of the operations is compromised / no more ensured.

title: Restriction, suspension of revocation of Aerodrome Certificate
text:
(a) Restriction, suspension or revocation of Aerodrome Certificate, could be due to  non-compliance
with the Aerodrome Certificate requirements or unresolved safety deficiency/concern including
inadequate resourcing, and in such cases the GCAA will notify the Aerodrome Operator  in writing
of its reasons.
(b) Revocation of an Aerodrome Certificate may be warranted if the Aerodrome Operator:
(1) is incapable or unwilling to carry out corrective action or has committed/repeated serious
violations; or
(2) has demonstrated a lack of responsibility, such as deliberate and flagrant acts of non -
compliance; or
(3) falsification of records jeopardizing aviation safety; or
(4) has made it convincingly clear that the continued operation of the aerodrome will be
detrimental to the public interest.

title: Transfer of Aerodrome Certificate
text:
(a) The current holder of the Aerodrome Certificate shall notify the GCAA in writing the following:
(1) before ceasing aerodrome operations of its intention and proposed date to cease
 operations;
(2) name and details of the proposed transferee.
(b) The proposed transferee shall apply to the GCAA as per the requirements of ADR.OR.C.010 -
Application for an Aerodrome Certificate, as applicable.
(c) The proposed transferee shall meet the appropriate requirements set out in in this CAR.
(d) The current holder of the Aerodrome Certificate and the proposed transferee shall notify the GCAA
at least 60 days in advance of the planned transfer date of the Aerodrome Certificate.

title: Transfer of Aerodrome Certificate
text:
Consent to the proposed transfer may be refused:
(a) if the GCAA is not satisfied that the proposed transferee will be able to operate and maintain the
aerodrome properly; or

(b) if significant changes to the operational aspects of the aerodrome will result or will be made by the
transferee (e.g. reduction in runway, taxiway or apron facilities; changes in the conditions of the
existing certificate unacceptable to the GCAA);
(c) inadequacy or inappropriateness of the new staffing arrangements or significant revisions to the
aerodrome manual;
(d) If the proposed transferee is not able to demonstrate that they meet the condition for holding an
Aerodrome Certificate as mentioned in this CAR.

title: Termination of operation
Termination of operation
text:
GENERAL
Upon the termination of the operation, the Aerodrome Operator  should apply closed runway markings
as mentioned in CS ADR-DSN. R.855 -Closed runways and taxiways, or parts thereof, as well as any other
measure  as directed by the GCAA.

title: Termination of operation
text:
The notification should be done at least three months in advance, so as to allow for the timely publication
of the changes, and their notification by the Aeronautical Information Regulation and Control (AIRAC)
system in accordance with the related timeframe.

title: Scope
text: Unless otherwise specified, the requirements of this subpart are applicable to land and water aerodromes.

title: Obligations for Landing Area Acceptance
text:
Prior to commencing the operation of an aerodrome, the Aerodrome Operator  as mentioned in
ADR.OR.D.010(b)  shall obtain the applicable Landing Area Acceptance issued by the GCAA.

title: Expression of interest for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
The applicant for a Landing Area Acceptance shall formally inform the GCAA  in writing of its interest to
develop and/or operate an aerodrome.

title: Expression interest for a Landing  Area Acceptance
text:
EXPRESSION OF INITIAL INTEREST
(a) The applicant for Landing Area Acceptance should arrange for a  meeting with the GCAA and provide
details of the proposed aerodrome site as well as concept of operations.
 The applicant should make arrangements for its key personnel to be present during this meeting.
During this meeting, the applicant should present to the GCAA its plans with regard to the
aerodrome.
(b) During the meeting, the applicant may be:
 (1) provided by the GCAA with general information about the applicable requirements  forthe
aerodrome to apply and obtain a  Landing Area Acceptance , such as need for Aerodrome
Registration, ownership details and point of contact, etc;
 (2) provided with copies of the applicable requirements, and a description of the procedures
 that are followed during the Landing Area Acceptance process; and
 (3) informed by the GCAA about possible approvals, permits, or clearances that may be
 needed  to be obtained from other authorities.
(4) Informed by the GCAA about the subsequent steps including – application for Regulatory
Design Review and application for aerodrome landing area acceptance once the construction
is completed.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
(a) Pursuant to the United Arab Emirates Federal Act No. 20 (1991) Promulgating The Civil Aviation Law
Article 27 and to the Civil Aviation Regulations (CARs) for the time being in force , a Landing Area
Acceptance (LAA) may be granted  by the GCAA, if it is s atisfied that an applicant is competent,
having regard to the applicant’s previous conduct and experience, the equipment, organisation,
staffing, maintenance and other arrangements, to ensure that the aerodrome and airspace are safe
for use by aircraft.
(b) The requirement for Landing Area Acceptance is as follows:
Aerodromes that are:
(1) not used for international flights;
(2) not used for air services (Note.- LAA may be provided for aerodromes used by light sports
aircraft only, when used for  air services);
(3) not available for instrument approaches or departure procedures.
(c) The applicant for a Landing Area Acceptance shall be the operator of the aerodrome who can be:
(1) the owner of the land on which the aerodrome is located;
(2) the occupier of the land on which the aerodrome is located; or
(3) the actual person or organisation operating the aerodrome and holding a formal consent
 from the owner or occupier of the land on which the facility is located.
(d) The application for an LAA and subsequent document submissions shall be made in a form and
manner established by the GCAA that includes no -objections certificates, approvals. Applicant for
LAA shall obtain approvals from GCAA in relation to Airspace and all relevant agencies, authorities
and entities including those mentioned in AMC2 ADR.OR.D.010(d).
(e) The applicant shall pay the applicable fees.
(f) The applicant shall provide the GCAA with the following:
(1) declaration of compliance and the completed compliance register;

(2) documentation demonstrating how it will comply with the applicable requirements. Such
documentation shall include a procedure, contained in the aerodrome manual, describing
how changes will be managed and notified to the GCAA; subsequent changes to these
procedures shall require prior approval by the GCAA.
(g) Applicant for Landing Area Acceptance shall demonstrate to the GCAA their compliance to the
requirements of CAR AGA, their arrangements for safeguarding of area within the OLS and beyond.
(h) The applicant shall satisfy the Landing Area Acceptance requirements at each stage of the
application process as detailed in the GM1 ADR.OR.D.010(h).
(i) The applicant of Landing Area Acceptance shall apply and obtain a no objection to the regulatory
design review and shall  not commence any construction activity until they receive a no -objection
to the  regulatory design review.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
(1) These aerodromes are characterised as private facilities not available for the general public
(excluding areas used solely for light sports aircraft);
(2) An operator of an aerodrome which is not intended for air service operations and does not have
instrument approach or departure procedures, may apply for an Aerodrome Certificate under these
regulations;
(3) For aerodromes which are listed as not Air Service operations (with non -instrument runways) and
issued with a Landing Area Acceptance, when extending their operations to an Air Service that
involve commercial operations or provide operations using inst rument approach or departure
procedures, then applicants shall apply for an Aerodrome Certificate, following the requirements
of this CAR.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
LANDING AREA ACCEPTANCE PROCESSING STAGES
Table OR-D- 1: Application for LAA – Processinig stages
Stage 1  Expression of Interest • Aerodrome Registration (see ADR.OR.C.010(c)
Registration of the organisation.)
Stage 2 Regulatory Design Review
(Applicant to apply for
Regulatory Design Review)
• Ownership (see ADR.OR.C.010(c) Relationship of
the applicant with the aerodrome owner).

• Security Clearance, Air space (see AMC2
ADR.OR.C.010(e)- other no-objections, approvals,
agreements and permissions).

• Compliance Matrix based on the CS in CAR AGA
PART ADR.

•  Drawings (see AMC1 ADR.OR.C.010(e) Application
for an Aerodrome Certificate).

• Met Studies (see AMC3 ADR.OR.C.010(e)
Meteorological study).

Stage 3 Aerodrome Certificate
(Upon completion of
construction, applicant to
apply for Aerodrome
Certificate)

applicable (See.AMC1 ADR.OR.C.010(f)).

SMS, Aerodrome Manual, AEP.

•  Certification Audit (including operations and
safety management).

• Post Audit submission of CAP by the applicant

• Issue of Certificate (see GM1 ADR.OR.C.010(i)
Issuance or refusal of Aerodrome Certificate.)

Note: Applicant for an aerodrome certificate may
