application, such as nomination of Post Holders;manual

acceptance (see AMC1 ADR.OR.C.010(e)(g) Aerodrome
manual, AEP, SMS) etc, ahead of the stage 3.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
RELATIONSHIP OF THE APPLICANT WITH THE AERODROME OWNER
(a) The applicant should provide the GCAA with all information necessary to demonstrate to the GCAA
its relationship with the aerodrome owner, and/or the owner of the land to be used for the
aerodrome development.
(b) Such documentation should include, but is not limited to, relevant portions of  contracts, lease
agreements, authorisations between the persons involved, etc.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
REGISTRATION  OF THE ORGANISATION
(a) Applicant should register their organization in the GCAA’s website, in order to make their
application through GCAA’s e-services or through other means established for this purpose by the
GCAA.
(b) Applicants should provide  evidence of their identity such as establishment / trade license
documentation and official documents as required during the registration process.
(c) Applicant should provide all documents and information as required in the application portal.
(d) Applicants should have secure access to the GCAA e -Services, available on the GCAA’s website:
www.gcaa.gov.ae. Applicants who do not have access to the GCAA’s e-Services must make an initial
request through GCAA’s customer service channels.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
INFORMATION TO BE PROVIDED TO THE GCAA FOR REGULATORY DESIGN REVIEW
(a) The location of the aerodrome, and its boundaries, including maps and charts to indicate various
facilities and area in the aerodrome.
 Maps should clearly indicate the aerodrome operational area which include, at least, runways,
taxiways, aprons, associated strips, runway end safety areas, stopways, clearways, aerodrome
visual aids, fixed aerodrome equipment, other aerodrome operational areas, areas adjacent to the
movement area. This defined area will be subject to aerodrome operations safety oversight by the
GCAA following the issue of Landing Area Acceptance .

 Aerodrome boundary should not be confused with the boundaries established for other purposes,
such as fences, the land ownership boundaries used by local planning authorities, or those used to
designate security restricted zones ,custom controlled areas, etc.
(b) The type of operations at the aerodrome including:
(1) the aircraft types to be served at the aerodrome, and the critical aircraft type to be used for
the design of the aerodrome;
(2) the type of approaches, landing, and/or take-off operations on each runway/FATO;
(3) operations during the day and/or night;
(4) operational concept and the associated airspace;
(5) any limitations to the operation of the aerodrome;
(6) the design and facilities of the aerodrome, in accordance with the applicable Certification
Specifications established by the GCAA;
(7) unmanned aircraft operations including fuelling and charging facilities.
(c) Information about the location of the aerodrome - the exact location of the aerodrome should be
depicted on a map of a suitable scale acceptable to the GCAA.
(d) Drawings in suitable scale , electronic format  acceptable to the GCAA should contain:
(1) orientation of Runway(s) / FATOs;
(2) the dimensions of the aerodrome’s physical characteristics;
(3) the visual and non-visual aids;
(4) the obstacle limitation surfaces, and any other surfaces applicable; and
(5) the aerodrome facilities, installations, and fixed equipment and their location.
(e) Description, height, and location of obstacles, in accordance with the applicable aeronautical data
requirements (see ADR.OPS. A.005).
(f) The applicant should identify the applicable Certification Specifications for the design and type of
operations of the proposed aerodrome and provide the GCAA with evidence that the proposed
design and operation complies with applicable regulations , the applicant should also provide the
GCAA with:
(1) the compliance register in the form and manner as established by the GCAA;

(2) the Certification Specifications for which it proposes to show compliance in a different
manner and demonstrate an equivalent level of safety. Such a proposal has to be acceptable
to the GCAA. In such cases, the applicant should also propose the method that will be used
to d emonstrate compliance and achieve an equivalent level of safety, and submit all
necessary documentation to support the proposal.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
OTHER NO-OBJECTIONS, APPROVALS AND PERMISSIONS
(a) A letter of no objection should be obtained from the Appropriate Authorities ensuring that the
necessary formal arrangements have been made with regard to the protection of the Obstacle
Limitation Surfaces (OLS).
(b) Applicants should obtain required approvals from other Appropriate Authorities (i.e. municipalities,
civil defense, local departments of civil aviation. Applicant should also establish coordination with
entities such as environmental agency, security agency as appropriate.
(c) `In addition to the application for a Landing Area Acceptance, other certification or approvals should
be required if Air Navigation Services such as ATS, CNS, MET and AIS is to be provided.
(d) Applicants may be required to apply for other certificates or approvals from the GCAA; this will be
dependent upon the scale and type of operations the aerodrome is intended to be used. Other
areas that require certification or approval are:
(1) Air Navigation Services:
  For the purposes of arrangements for Air Navigation services.
(2) Airspace:
For the purpose of ensuring the suitability of the proposed site from an airspace perspective,
taking into consideration the proximity of the aerodrome to other aerodromes and landing
sites, including military aerodromes; obstacles and terrain; any excessi ve operational
restriction requirements; any existing restrictions such as – special use airspace,  controlled
airspace; and any existing flight procedures.
(3) Aviation Security:
(A) Security clearance to confirm that supporting resources and facilities required by
aviation security services are made available at facilities serving civil aviation.

(B) Applicants should, prior to the issue of a Regulatory Design Review  and for aviation
activity, obtain a security clearance from GCAA through the established means.
(e) There may also be other bodies that the applicants should inform in their own interests and it is the
responsibility of the Aerodrome Operator  to obtain the appropriate approvals. The application for
planning/building permissions and the request for a Landing Area Acceptance  are not
interdependent and are required to be made separately.
(f) As a part of the Landing Area Acceptance process, the physical characteristics and design should
consider, where appropriate, land-use and environmental control measures.
(g) Previously issued approvals, if any, will generally be reassessed each 12 months if there are delays
or extended periods of inactivity.
(h) Applicant should have arrangement (MOU or agreement) with the AIS to ensure up -to-date
information of aerodrome safety-related conditions are published.

title: Application for a  Landing Area Acceptance
text:
METEOROLOGICAL STUDY
The applicant should have details of the study of the area of the aerodrome, including temperature,
visibility, ceiling and wind conditions; moreover, the study should provide information on wind conditions
occurring with poor visibility and/or low cloud base at the aerodrome, and their frequency, as well as the
accompanying wind direction and speed.
For Meteorological requirements refer to CAR ANS- PART MET- AERONAUTICAL METEOROLOGY SERVICE
PROVIDERS.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
REGULATORY DESIGN REVIEW
(a) GCAA’s  Regulatory Design Review  is based on the assessment of the information provided by the
applicant and  is valid for a period of one year. If construction of the aerodrome has not been
commenced by that time, the applicant should request for an extension of the Regulatory Design
Review  to ensure that the proposal remains in compliance with GCAA Regulations.
(b) The issue of a  no-objection by the GCAA for the Regulatory Design Review  does not permit the
aerodrome to be used for operations until when construction is completed and a Landing Area
Acceptance is obtained from the GCAA.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
APPLICABLE FEES
Service fees, as published on the GCAA’s website are varied from time to time and should be paid to the
GCAA:
(a) during the initial Landing Area Acceptance ; and
(b) on a periodic basis after the grant of a Landing Area Acceptance;
for each aerodrome.
Note.- Payment of the GCAA’s service fee does not guarantee the grant or continuation for aerodrome
operations  or of a Landing Area Acceptance.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
AERODROME MANUAL, AEP, SMS
(a) The manuals mentioned below and their amendments should be submitted to the GCAA in
electronic format that allows the GCAA to review, store, and reproduce it.
(1) an electronic version of the aerodrome manual, as required by ADR.OR.B.005 - Aerodrome
Manual , including the aerodrome manual checklist;
(2) an electronic version of the Aerodrome Operator ’s Safety Management System (SMS)
manual as required by CAR SMS ,including a SMS manual checklist;
(3) an electronic version of the Aerodrome Emergency Plan (AEP) as required by Part ACM,
including an AEP manual checklist.
(b) The GCAA will evaluate and verify if :
(1) the aerodrome manual contains all pertinent information on the aerodrome site, facilities,
services, equipment, operating procedures, organization and management;
(2) the Aerodrome Operator’s Safety Management System and supporting operating procedures
make satisfactory provision for the safety of aircraft;
(3) the aerodrome Rescue Firefighting Service is staffed, trained, equipped, operated and
organised to the meet the applicable requirements.

title: Application for a  Landing Area Acceptance
text:
ADEQUACY OF STRUCTURE AND RESOURCES
(a) The applicant should provide all necessary information needed in order to demonstrate to the
GCAA that its proposed organisation and management are suitable, and properly matched to the
scale and scope of the operation.
(b) Evidence of adequacy of resources to operate the aerodrome in accordance with  ADR.OR.A.030-
Personnel requirements- Landing Area Acceptance, to enable the GCAA to assess each nominated
aerodrome Post Holder based on the assessment criteria as established in this CAR.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
ASSESSMENTS AND  EVALUATIONS
(a) The GCAA’s assessments, site visits and inspections will assess inter -alia physical characteristics,
visual aids (markings, lights, signs and markers), obstacle environment ;
(b) Before granting a Landing Area Acceptance, the GCAA may verify that:
(1) the aerodrome’s facilities, services ,equipment and systems are in accordance with the Civil
Aviation Regulations and further to review, inspection or verification audit;
(2) the Aerodrome Operator ’s processes and procedures as referenced in the Aerodrome
Manual;
(3) the applicant’s ability to operate and maintain the aerodrome properly.
(c) The applicant should provide the GCAA, documentation to demonstrate how it will comply with the
applicable requirements of this CAR and any other applicable requirements.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
ISSUANCE OR REFUSAL OF A LANDING AREA ACCEPTANCE
(a) The GCAA will only issue a Landing Area Acceptance , when it is completely satisfied that all
regulatory and critical safety elements have been adequately addressed; this may require a further
GCAA audit / inspection follow-up visit and / or special additional operating approvals. This includes
evidence of any prior approvals or permissions.
(b) The GCAA may impose operating restrictions and/or sanctions at an aerodrome.
(c) After completion of the processing of the application, the GCAA while granting the Landing Area
Acceptance, may endorse the conditions of the type of use of the aerodrome and other details as
shown in the Landing Area Acceptance.

(d) In the event of non -compliance with the requirements of this CAR or unresolved safety
deficiencies/concerns, the GCAA may refuse to grant a Landing Area Acceptance, in such cases, will
notify the applicant in writing of its reasons.

title: Application for a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
TIMESCALE FOR PROCESSING OF APPLICATIONS
(a) It is important that applicants submit the required documents sufficiently early to allow for detailed
consideration of the application and site inspection if required.
(b) The GCAA cannot undertake to reach a decision within a particular timescale or to meet a
commercial deadline set by the applicant.

title: Application for Landing Area Acceptance
text:
LANDING AREA ACCEPTANCE
( Intentionally left blank)

title: Application for Landing Area Acceptance
text:
GENERAL - AERODROME NAMING AND ALLOCATION OF ICAO CODE
(a) The naming of an aerodrome is directly connected with aeronautical communications and flight
safety information. It is therefore important that aerodrome is representative of its location (the
nearest city, town or village) and should not have the potentia l to be confused with another
aerodrome.
(b) Aerodrome operator should apply to the GCAA for assignment of four -letter ICAO code. The
decision to assign a code for the aerodrome and get it validated through ICAO will remain with the
GCAA and is subject to confirmation by ICAO.
(c) ICAO Document 7910 - Location Identifiers contains codes allocated by national governments on
behalf of ICAO, to airports, airfields and other facilities such as ATC and weather stations.

title: Scope of the Landing Area Acceptance
text: An Aerodrome Operator  shall comply with the scope and conditions of the Landing Area Acceptance.

title: Continued validity of a Landing Area Acceptance
text:
(a) The GCAA may only grant and permit a Landing Area Acceptance to continue where it is satisfied
that the Aerodrome Operator  can ensure that the aerodrome and its airspace are safe for use by
aircraft.

(b) Unless renewed , a Landing Area Acceptance shall remain valid for a period of three years from the
date of issue of a Landing Area Acceptance subject to:
(1) the Aerodrome Operator  remaining in compliance with the relevant requirements of this
CAR, and other applicable regulations and the aerodrome remaining in compliance with their
compliance register;
(2) the satisfactory outcome of regulatory surveillance activities;
(3) the Aerodrome Operator’s handling of findings as specified under ADR.OR.J.020 -Findings
and corrective actions, to the satisfaction of the GCAA;
(4) the GCAA being granted access to the Aerodrome Operator ’s organisation as defined in

-Granting of access, to determine continued compliance with the relevant
requirements of this CAR;
(5) the aerodrome operations are conducted within the scope and conditions as detailed in the
Landing Area Acceptance;
(6) the Landing Area Acceptance not being surrendered or revoked;
(7) Payment of all applicable service fees as published by the GCAA.
(c) The validity of the Landing Area Acceptance is based upon the physical characteristics, type of use
of the aerodrome and continued operation in accordance with the GCAA Publications.
(d) Any change made to the physical characteristics, compliance register or use of the aerodrome, as
documented in the aerodrome manual that is not accepted by the GCAA shall invalidate the Landing
Area Acceptance.
(e) Upon revocation or surrender, the Landing Area Acceptance shall be returned to the GCAA without
delay.

title: Amendment to Landing Area Acceptance
text:
Aerodrome operator shall submit the following with any request for amendment in Landing Area
Acceptance:
(a) detailed account of the proposed amendment including the reasons for the amendment;
(b) an assessment of the safety risks associated with any change in use or operation of the aerodrome
including, where appropriate, the findings of any aeronautical study undertaken on behalf of the
operator;

(c) particulars of any consequential changes to the AIP, aerodrome manual and aerodrome emergency
plan; and
(d) Any other request as notified by the GCAA.

title: Amendment to Landing Area Acceptance
Restriction, suspension of revocation of Landing Area Acceptance
text:
Federal Act 20 - Article 27 provides that the GCAA may, on sufficient safety grounds revoke or suspend a
Landing Area Acceptance.
The Landing Area Acceptance  shall be restricted, suspended or revoked by the GCAA , if in the view of
the GCAA, the safety of the operations is compromised / no more ensured.

title: Restriction, suspension of revocation of Landing Area Acceptance
text:
(a) Restriction,  suspension, or revocation of a  Landing Area Acceptance,  could be due to  non-
compliance with the Landing Area Acceptance requirements or unresolved safety deficiency/concern
including inadequate resourcing , and in such cases the GCAA will notify the Aerodrome Operator  in
writing of its reasons.
(b) Revocation of an Aerodrome Certificate may be warranted if the Aerodrome Operator:
(1) is incapable or unwilling to carry out corrective action or has committed/repeated serious
violations; or

(2) has demonstrated a lack of responsibility, such as deliberate and flagrant acts of non -
compliance; or
(3) falsification of records jeopardizing aviation safety; or
(4) has made it convincingly clear that the continued operation of the aerodrome will be
detrimental to the public interest.

title: Transfer of Landing Area Acceptance
text:
(a) The current holder of the Landing Area Acceptance shall notify the GCAA in writing the following:
(1) before ceasing aerodrome operations of its intention and proposed date to cease operations;
(2) name and details of the proposed transferee.
(b) The proposed transferee shall apply to the GCAA as per the requirements of ADR.OR.D.10 -
Application for a Landing Area Acceptance, as applicable.
(c) The proposed transferee shall meet the requirements set out in in this CAR.
(d) The current holder of the Landing Area Acceptance and the proposed transferee shall notify the
GCAA at least 60 days in advance of the planned transfer date of the Landing Area Acceptance.

title: Transfer of Landing Area Acceptance
text:
Consent to the proposed transfer may be refused
(a) if the GCAA is not satisfied that the proposed transferee will be able to operate and maintain the
aerodrome properly; or
(b) if significant changes to the operational aspects of the aerodrome will result or will be made by the
transferee (e.g. reduction in runway, taxiway or apron facilities; changes in the conditions of the
existing certificate unacceptable to the GCAA);or
(c) inadequacy or inappropriateness of the new staffing arrangements or significant revisions to the
aerodrome manual).

title: Termination of operation- Landing Area Acceptance
Termination of operation- Landing Area Acceptance
text:
GENERAL
Upon the termination of the operation, the Aerodrome Operator should apply closed runway markings as
mentioned in CS ADR -DSN.R.855-Closed runways and taxiways, or parts thereof, as well as any other
measure as directed by the  GCAA.

title: Termination of operation- Landing Area Acceptance
text:
The notification should be done at least three months in advance, so as to allow for the timely publication
of the changes, and their notification by the Aeronautical Information Regulation and Control (AIRAC)
system in accordance with the related timeframe.

title: CONTRACTING OF ACTIVITIES (ADR.OR. E)
text: Note : This section is applicable for certified aerodromes only

title: Contracting of activities
text:
(a) When the Aerodrome Operator  decides to contract fully, its activities and/or services  (hereby
known as the ‘contracted activities or services’) on a temporary or permanent basis to another
organisation (hereby known as the ‘contracted organisation’) then it shall be subject to the
following requirements:
(1) Aerodrome Operator  shall obtain prior approval from GCAA when activities and/or
services that is under the scope of the Aerodrome Certificate, are fully contracted to
another organisation, on a temporary or permanent basis;
(2) Aerodrome Operator  shall submit to the GCAA the Management of Change (see CAR

Management of Change) and the transition plan,  prior to contracting the
activities and/or services to another organisation, on a temporary or permanent basis.
(b) When the Aerodrome Operator  decides to contract portion its activities and/or services (hereby
known as the ‘contracted activities or services’) on a temporary or permanent basis to another
organisation (hereby known as the ‘contracted organisation’) then it shall be subject to the
following requirements:
(1) Aerodrome Operator  shall notify the GCAA about its decision to contract  a portion of any
activities and / or / services on a temporary or permanent basis, that is under the scope of
the Aerodrome Certificate;
(2) Aerodrome Operator  shall submit to the GCAA the Management of change (see CAR

Management of Change) and the transition plan,  prior to contracting the
activities and/or services to another organisation, on a temporary or permanent basis.
(c) The relationship between the Aerodrome Operator  and contracted organisations shall be defined
on the service agreement of both organisations and they shall comply with any conditions stated
in their respective service agreement.
(d) The Aerodrome Operator  shall within its management system:
(1) have a procedure which includes management of change , transition planning , risk
management. performance monitoring and compliance oversight  including:

i. definition of  relevant management responsibilities within its own organisation
regarding oversight and monitoring of the contracted organisation;
ii. assurance that the contracted organisation effectively conducts the contracted
activities and / or services , and confirms to the applicable requirements; and
iii. assurance that the contracted organisation has implemented appropriate elements of
safety management and quality assurance systems  including but not limited to
mechanisms to remedy any immediate hazards to satisfy and rectify situations that
could lower safety standards.
(e) Regardless of their certification status, the contracted organisation shall:
(1) work under the oversight system of the Aerodrome Operator;
(2) comply with terms of the aerodrome and its certification requirements.
(f) The ultimate responsibility and accountability for the activities and / or services provided by the
contracted organisation shall remain with the Aerodrome Operator.
(g) The Aerodrome Operator  shall ensure that:
(1) all contracted activities and / or services are subject to appropriate  elements  of  safety
management and quality assurance system established by the Aerodrome Operator;
(2) any identified deficiencies and/ or audit findings against the contracted organisation are
resolved through the processes as required by the GCAA.
(h) The Aerodrome Operator  shall ensure that the GCAA is given full unrestricted access to the
contracted organisation, to determine continued compliance with the applicable requirements.

title: Contracted activities
text:
GENERAL - RESPONSIBILITY WHEN CONTRACTING ACTIVITIES
When an  Aerodrome Operator decides to contract fully its activities and/or  services to another
organisation:
(a) a formal agreement should exist between the Aerodrome Operator and the contracted
organisation, clearly defining the contracted activities and / or services  and the applicable
requirements including training and competencies requirements for personnel employed by the
contracted organisation where applicable;

(b) the contracted safety related activities and / or services  relevant to the agreement should be
included in the Aerodrome Operator ’s safety management  and compliance monitoring
programmes;
(c) the Aerodrome Operator should ensure that the contracted organisation has the necessary
resources, authorisation, declaration, or approval when required and commands the resources
and competence to undertake the task; to this end, a prior audit of the contracted party should
be conducted to ensure that the contracted organisation meets the applicable requirements, and
the requirements specified by the Aerodrome Operator  itself.

title: Contracted activities
text:
RESPONSIBILITY WHEN CONTRACTING ACTIVITIES AND/OR SERVICES
(a) Where contracted activities and/or services involve aircraft movement areas, the Aerodrome
Operator should carry out additional oversight activity to ensure that the activities and/or services
are carried out in safe and effective manner.

title: Contracted activities
Aerodrome operator responsibilities
text:
(a) The Aerodrome Operator is responsible for the safe operation and maintenance of the aerodrome
in accordance with:
(1) CAR AGA and other relevant publications by the GCAA including but not limiting to Safety
Decisions, Safety Alerts and any other relevant CARs that are applicable to aerodromes and
Aerodrome Operators;
(2) the standard conditions, scope and specific conditions of aerodrome  certificate and landing
area acceptance;
(3) the content of the aerodrome manual; and
(4) any other document as applicable.
(b) The Aerodrome Operator shall ensure directly, or coordinate through  formal arrangements as
required:
(1) for providing the air navigation services appropriate to the level of traffic and  the operating
conditions at the aerodrome;
(2) for Aeronautical Information Service (AIS);
(3) for meteorology services as stated in CAR ANS- PART MET- AERONAUTICAL METEOROLOGY
SERVICE PROVIDERS;
(4) for obstacle control; and
(5) aerodrome safeguarding activities, as applicable.
(c) The Aerodrome Operator shall coordinate with the AIS to ensure that relevant information for the
safety of aircraft that is contained in the aerodrome manual is published where appropriate. This
shall include:
(1) provisions for which an equivalent level of safety that was accepted by the GCAA;
(2) special conditions and limitations with regard to the use of the aerodrome.

(d) If an unsafe condition develops at the aerodrome, the Aerodrome Operator shall, without undue
delay, take all necessary measures to ensure that those parts of the aerodrome found to endanger
safety are not used by aircraft.
(e) The Aerodrome Operator, in order to ensure the safe operation of aircraft at the aerodrome, shall
provide and maintain, directly or through formal arrangements with third parties, appropriate
infrastructure, visual and non-visual aids for – navigation, to denote obstacles, restricted use area,
meteorological equipment and any other equipment, commensurate with the type of operations
conducted at the aerodrome and comply with the specification in this CAR and other relevant CARs.
(f) Aerodrome operators shall stipulate requirements , and en sure that  ground handling service
providers implement and maintain a Safety Management System that is commensurate with the
size and complexity of their operation and to actively participate in the Aerodrome Operator’s SMS.
(g) Aerodrome operators shall establish an internal quality assurance system to ensure compliance
with, and the adequacy of CAR AGA ,and for the continued improvement of safety levels.
(h) Aerodrome operator shall provide statistical and other operational information as requested by the
GCAA.
(i) The Aerodrome Operator shall require  and ensure all the users of the aerodrome including fixed-
base operators and organisations which perform activities independently at the aerodrome, related
to, or in direct support of, the safe operation of aircraft to comply with the requirements laid down
by the Aerodrome Operator with regard to safety and order at the aerodromes, and shall monitor
such compliance.
(j) The Aerodrome Operator shall when necessary for the safety of aircraft operations, establish any
limitations on the use of the aerodrome that arise from the aerodrome design or the facilities or
services provided at the aerodrome, which shall be recorded in the aerodrome manual and
communicated to the air navigation service provider and aeronautical information services
provider.
(k) The Aerodrome Operator shall ensure that procedures are developed to negate aircraft operators
from operating at their aerodrome when such aircraft operators cannot meet the UAE regulatory
requirements, or are subject to:
(1) a ban based upon the origin of registry as notified by the GCAA; or

(2) a cease and desist order as notified by the GCAA; or
(3) when the aircraft is subject to a grounding order as notified by the GCAA.

title: Aerodrome operator responsibilities
text:
INFORMATION TO THE AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES AND OTHER ENTITIES
Aerodrome operator should provide without any delay:
(a) a description of cases of equivalent level of safety, special conditions, including limitations with
regard to the use of the aerodrome, should be published in the Aeronautical Information
Publication (AIP), after coordination with the GCAA;
(b) information to the AIS provider, of any changes in the operational status or availability of the
published aerodrome infrastructure.

title: Aerodrome operator responsibilities
text:
STATISTICAL AND OTHER OPERATIONAL INFORMATION
The Aerodrome Operator should also provide the following statistical information to the ICAO with copy
to the GCAA:
(a) monthly airport traffic statistics: ICAO Form I should be completed and forwarded via e -mail on a
monthly basis;
(b) annual airport traffic statistics: ICAO Form I -S should be completed and forward via e -mail on an
annual basis.

title: Aerodrome operator responsibilities
text:
Templates for the ICAO forms are located at https://www.icao.int/sustainability/Pages/eap-sta-
excel.aspx; Forms should be sent to stats@aci.aero with a copy to stats@gcaa.gov.ae

title: Aerodrome operator responsibilities
text:
Aerodrome operators should ensure that they:
(a) maintain their safety responsibilities over safety related activities conducted by those third -party
organisations related to, or in direct support of, the safe and secure operation of aircraft;

(b) have the power to access and inspect any third -party organisations providing a service related to,
or in direct support of, the safe and secure operation of aircraft operating from the aerodrome
including its facilities and records to determine continued c ompliance with the relevant
requirements through safety audits or inspections. The scope of the services provided and the
Aerodrome Operator ’s power to access and inspect should be included in the contractual
arrangement; and
(c) are able to impose operating restrictions in the event of non-compliance with the applicable safety
and security requirements or unresolved safety or security deficiencies or concerns.

title: Aerodrome operator responsibilities
text:
OBLIGATIONS TO RESTRICT CERTAIN AIRCRAFT
(a) The Aerodrome Operator ’s procedures should include immediate notification to the GCAA of
actions taken against such aircraft or aircraft operators.
(b) The Aerodrome Operator should monitor and ensure that third parties at the aerodrome comply
with such procedures.

title: Granting of access
text:
For the purpose of determining compliance with the relevant requirements, an Aerodrome Operator  shall
grant access to any person authorised by the GCAA to:
(a) any facility, document, records, data, procedures or any other material relevant to its activity
subject to certification or declaration, whether it is contracted or not; and
(b) perform or witness any action, inspection, test, assessment or exercise that the  GCAA finds as
necessary.

title: Occurrence reporting
text:
(a) The Aerodrome Operator shall establish procedures for the notification, investigation, and
reporting of safety events to the GCAA and adhere to the requirements established in CAR  OCR.
(b) The Aerodrome Operator shall report to the GCAA, any accident, serious incident and occurrences.
In accordance with CAR OCR.

(c) Without prejudice to point (b), the Aerodrome Operator shall report to the GCAA, any malfunction,
technical defects, exceeding of technical limitations, occurrence or other irregular circumstances
that has or may have endangered the safety of the operations and that has not resulted in an
accident or serious incident.
(d) Aerodrome operators shall establish procedures to carry out investigation as defined in CAR SMS.

title: Occurrence reporting
text:
GENERAL- REPORTING PROCEDURES
The Aerodrome Operator should establish procedures to be used for reporting to the GCAA, as required,
which include at least:
 the description of the applicable requirements for the purpose of reporting;
 the description of the reporting mechanism, including reporting forms, means, and deadlines;
 the personnel responsible for reporting; and
 the description of the mechanism and personnel responsibilities for identifying root causes, and the
actions that may be needed to be taken to prevent similar occurrences from happening in the
future, as appropriate.

title: (b)(c) Occurrence reporting
text:
REPORTING OF INCIDENT TO THE GCAA
 The Aerodrome Operator should submit all reportable occurrences as defined in CAR OCR or unless
specific alternative provisions are requested by the GCAA.
 Reports should be made via the GCAA ROSI (Reporting of Safety Incident) System applicable to
aerodromes and/or any other reporting  system as established by the GCAA.
 Reports should be made as soon as possible and in any case within the relevant notification period
defined in CAR OCR, unless otherwise instructed by the GCAA.

title: (b)(c)Occurrence reporting
text:
WILDLIFE STRIKE REPORTING
In the event of a wildlife strike including bird strike, the Aerodrome Operator should use the ROSI system
or any other system as established by the GCAA to make mandatory reports to the GCAA.

title: Voluntary reporting system
text:
An Aerodrome Operator  shall establish a system to educate their personnel of how to report an actual or
potential safety deficiency through the GCAA’s Voluntary Reporting System (VORSY)  or any other such
system established by the GCAA.

title: Voluntary reporting system
text:
It is recognised that a mature safety culture will support healthy internal reporting and will rarely require
issues to be raised external to the organisation. Nevertheless, there should be no documentation,
publication, or actions that discourage, directly or indirectly, the use of the VORSY external reporting
system.

title: Prevention of fire
Airport design and master plan
text:
(a) A master plan containing detailed plans for the development of aerodrome infrastructure shall be
established for aerodrome.
(b) The master plan shall:
(1) contain a schedule of priorities including a phased implementation plan; and
(2) be reviewed periodically to consider current and future aerodrome traffic.
(c) The design of aerodromes shall consider, where appropriate land-use, and environmental control
measures and aerodrome land reserves, safeguarding measures.
(d) Architectural and infrastructure -related requirements for the optimum implementation of
international civil aviation security measures shall be integrated into the design and construction
of new facilities and alterations to existing facilities at an aerodrome.
(e) Aerodrome stakeholders, particularly aircraft operators, air navigation service providers, shall be
identified and be consulted in order to facilitate the master planning process using a consultative
and collaborative approach.

title: Airport design and master plan
text:
(a) A master plan for the long-term development of an aerodrome displays the ultimate development
in a phased manner and reports the data and logic upon which the plan is based. Master plans are
prepared to support modernization of existing aerodromes and crea tion of new aerodromes,
regardless of size, complexity, and role. It is important to note that a master plan does not
constitute a confirmed implementation programme. It provides information on the types of
improvements to be undertaken in a phased manner.
Note 1 .- Provision of advanced planning data to facilitate the planning process include future aircraft
types, characteristics and numbers of aircraft expected to be used, the anticipated growth of
aircraft movements, number of passengers and amount of cargo projected to be handled.
Note 2.- Guidance in Annex 9, Chapter 6 on the need for aircraft operators to inform Aerodrome Operator
s concerning the former’s service, schedule and fleet plans to enable rational planning of facilities
and services in relation to the traffic anticipated.

Note 3.- Guidance in ICAO's Policies on Charges for Airports and Air Navigation Services Doc 9082), Section
1, regarding consultation with users concerning provision of advance planning data and protection
of commercially sensitive data.
(b) A master plan should represent the development plan of a specific aerodrome. It should be
developed based on economic feasibility, traffic forecasts, current and future requirements
provided by, among others, aircraft operators.
(c) After completing the master plan, the concerned organisation must then take the broad guidelines
of the master plan and translate them into a programme that recognizes the specific airport
constraints and opportunities presented. This programme would typic ally be translated into a 5 -
year capital investment programme as part of a larger 10 -year rolling capital plan in close
consultation with airport users.
(d) To ensure a realistic and appropriate fit to continuously evolving aviation industry conditions, the
master plan should be reviewed in its entirety every 5 years, or more often if changes in economic,
operational, environmental and financial conditions war rant an earlier revision. Adjustments may
need to be made to assumptions used during the initial master plan process, including phasing and
ongoing airfield and facility development as air transport evolves.
(e) A master plan represents the development plan of a specific aerodrome . It is developed by the
Aerodrome Operator  based on economic feasibility, traffic forecasts, and current and future
requirements provided by, among others, aircraft operators.
(f) A master plan may be required when the lack of capacity at an airport, due to conditions such as,
but not limited to expected traffic growth, changing weather and climatic conditions or major works
to address safety or environmental concerns, would put the connectivity of a geographical area at
risk or cause severe disruption to the air transport network.

title: Management system
text:
(a) The Aerodrome Operator  holding an Aerodrome Certificate shall implement and maintain a
management system including a Safety Management System ,to comply with all the requirements
of CAR SMS and their Quality Assurance System.
(b) The management system shall include:
(1) clearly defined lines of responsibility and accountability throughout the Aerodrome
Operator , including a direct accountability for safety on the part of senior management;
(2) a description of the overall principles and policies of the Aerodrome Operator  with regard
to safety, referred to as the safety policy, signed by the accountable manager;
(3) a formal process that ensures that hazards in operations are identified and reported;
(4) a formal process that ensures analysis, assessment and mitigation of the safety risks in
aerodrome operations and remedial actions necessary to maintain acceptable level of safety
is implemented;
(5) the means to verify the safety performance of the Aerodrome Operator’s organisation in
reference to the safety performance indicators and safety performance targets of the
safety management system, and to validate the effectiveness of safety risk controls;
(6) a formal process to:
(i) identify and manage changes within the Aerodrome Operator’s  organisation,
management system, the aerodrome or its operation which may affect established
processes, procedures, services and aircraft operations;
(ii) describe the arrangements to ensure safety performance before implementing
changes; and
(iii) eliminate or modify safety risk controls that are no longer needed or effective due to
changes in the operational environment;

(7) a formal process to review the management system referred to in paragraph (a),
identify the causes of substandard performance of the safety management system,
determine the implications of such substandard performance in operations, and
eliminate or mitigate such causes;
(8) a safety training programme that ensures that personnel involved in the operation,
rescue and firefighting, maintenance and management of the aerodrome are trained and
competent to perform their duties as specified in the organisation’s SMS requirements;
(9) formal means for safety communication that ensures that personnel are fully aware of
the safety management system, conveys safety critical information, and explains why
particular safety actions are taken and why safety procedures are introduced or changed;
(10) coordination of the Safety Management System with the aerodrome emergency response
plan; and coordination of the aerodrome emergency response plan with the emergency
response plans of those organisations it must interface with during the provision of
aerodrome services; and
(11) a formal proces s  to monitor compliance of the organisation with the relevant
requirements.
(c) The Aerodrome Operator  shall document all management system key processes.
(d) The management system shall be proportionate to the size of the organisation and its activities,
taking into account the hazards and associated risks inherent in these activities.
(e) The Aerodrome Operator  shall organise, coordinate and implement safety programmes to
promote safety at the aerodrome.  Such programmes should include, but are not limited to:
(1) runway, taxiway safety and incursion prevention;
(2) apron safety; and
(3) FOD prevention.

title: Management system
text:
THE QUALITY ASSURANCE SYSTEM
(a) Aerodrome operator should establish a quality assurance system that is:

(1) continual, incorporating inspections, audits, and reviews to assess the adequacy of controls
in key programmes and systems;
(2) ongoing, identifying deficiencies, developing corrective and preventive action plans to
correct those deficiencies, and performing follow-up reviews.

title: Management system
text: (a) Aerodrome operators holding Landing Area Acceptance should endeavour to comply with

Management system (a) and shall in any case implement and maintain a
management system that is commensurate with the size of its operations and acceptable to the
GCAA.
(b) The Aerodrome Operator  holding a Landing Area Acceptance:
(1) may replace the safety review board with any other appropriate forums;
(2) may include SMS as a component of the aerodrome manual.

title: Management system
text:
THE  QUALITY ASSURANCE SYSTEM
(a) The GCAA encourages organisations to extend their quality assurance system beyond regulatory
compliance to determine the areas needing enhancement  in operations. Based on these
determinations organisations can enhance operating practices before deficiencies occur and help
embed an organisational culture which prioritises continuous improvement.
(b) the most effective QMSs are those where all staff, not only management and the Quality Assurance
(QA) team, understand the QMS, its importance and their role in maintaining it.
  All staff and managers have a part to play in ensuring that an organisation’s policies and procedures
provide for safety compliance, meet quality standards and allow individuals to perform work
properly. This is achieved by continuously monitoring an orga nisation’s performance and safety
standards as part of normal work activities and ensuring that operations are safe and in compliance
with the rules.
(c) Aerodrome operator’s Internal quality assurance system does not replace GCAA’s monitoring
activities.

title: Management system
Management system
text:
SMS AND QMS
(a) SMS and QMS share a number of common purposes and processes:
(1) both depend upon measuring and monitoring;
(2) both strive for continuous improvement;
(3) both use some of the same tools, such as auditing and review.
(b) However, a QAS does not include all the elements, features and activities of an SMS, as it focuses
mainly on compliance, conformance and monitoring. SMS goes further and requires the
organisation to identify and manage risk to achieve an acceptable level of safety performance. It is
not so much a case of replacing QMS by SMS, but instead, realising that they are complementary
and inextricably linked. An effective SMS can be built by applying QMS principles.

title: Management system
text:
COMPONENTS OF QUALITY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Main components of a QMS
(a) Quality Control Planning - Identifying quality goals and standards, the requirements necessary to
meet them, and the procedures to be used to check that they are being met.
(b) Quality Control - Physically inspecting and testing what was laid out in the planning stage to make
sure it is meets the desired outcomes.
(c) Internal Quality Assurance (IQA) - Reviewing the delivery process of services or the quality
management of operations.
(d) Quality Improvement- Thoroughly reviewing the findings from the above three components, with
the aim of improving methods in the future.

title: Management system
text:
SAFETY PERFORMANCE MONITORING AND MEASUREMENT
The Aerodrome Operator  should define levels of safety that should be expressed in the following two
terms:
(a) Safety Performance Indicators;

(b) Safety Performance Targets.
Safety Performance Targets should be supported by an action plan.

title: Management system
Management system
text:
SAFETY PERFORMANCE MONITORING AND MEASUREMENT
Aerodrome operator should define periodic Safety Performance Targets for each of the following incident
classifications:
(a) Runway Incursions - CAT A/CAT B;
(b) Runway Incursion - CAT C/CAT D;
(c) Manoeuvring Area Excursion - CAT A/CAT C (related to Runway); and

(d) FOD Incident resulting in Aircraft Damage (any category).

title: Management system
text:
SAFETY PERFORMANCE MONITORING AND MEASUREMENT- CATEGORIES OF INCIDENTS
Manoeuvering Area
Excursion CAT A
An incident in which an aircraft has an excursion from a runway – i.e.
overruns, excursion off the side of the runway – resulting in damage to
aircraft.
Manoeuvering Area
Excursion CAT B
An incident in which an aircraft has an excursion from a taxiway – excursion
off the side of the taxiway – resulting in damage to aircraft.
Manoeuvering Area
Excursion CAT C
An incident in which an aircraft has an excursion from a runway – i.e.
overruns, excursion off the side of the runway – resulting in no damage to
aircraft.
Manoeuvering Area
Excursion CAT D
An incident in which an aircraft has an excursion from a taxiway- excursion
off the side of the taxiway – resulting in no damage to aircraft.
Runway Incursion
CAT A A serious incident in which a collision is narrowly avoided.
Runway Incursion
CAT B
A runway incursion in which the separation decreases and there is a
significant potential for collision, which may result in a time-critical
corrective/evasive response to avoid a collision. This includes a runway
incursion occurring while a departing aircraft has commenced its take-off roll
or an arriving aircraft has crossed the threshold.
Runway Incursion
CAT C
A runway incursion characterized by ample time and/or distance to avoid a
collision, including a runway incursion occurring while a departing aircraft
has been cleared to line up, or cleared for take-off or an arriving aircraft has
been cleared to land but has not crossed the threshold.
Runway Incursion
CAT D
A runway incursion that meets the definition of a runway incursion such as
the incorrect presence of a vehicle, person or aircraft on the protected area
of a surface designated for the landing and take-off of aircraft but with no
immediate safety consequences.
FOD CAT A FOD which is likely to cause damage to an aircraft on a runway or runway
shoulder.
FOD CAT B FOD which is likely to cause damage to an aircraft found within runway strip
or RESA.
FOD CAT C FOD which is likely to cause damage to an aircraft on taxiways or taxiway
shoulders.
FOD CAT D FOD which is likely to cause damage to an aircraft found on the taxiway
strips, apron areas or elsewhere on the airfield.
Bird/Wildlife
Incident CAT A
 An incident where a pilot experiences wildlife striking an aircraft resulting in
significant damage to the aircraft and or requiring an aborted take-off, in-
flight diversion, prioritized landing or resulting in an accident.
Bird/Wildlife
Incident CAT B
An incident where a pilot reports an actual or potential wildlife strike, which
does not result in significant damage or adversely affect the flight.
Damage to Aircraft
CAT A Destroyed – Aircraft is unlikely to ever fly again – total write off.
Damage to Aircraft
CAT B
Substantially Damaged – Major damage that prevents the aircraft from flight
until significant maintenance is undertaken.

title: Management system
Management system
Management system
text:
COORDINATION OF THE AERODROME EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN
The coordination of the aerodrome emergency response plan, established in accordance with the
requirements contained in this CA R, with the safety management system , should ensure continuous
improvement of the systems and procedures contained within the plan.

title: Management system
text:
COORDINATION OF THE AERODROME EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN
Continuous improvement of the systems and procedures contained within the aerodrome emergency
response plan may, amongst others, be obtained by:

(a) conducting a review of the relevant parts of the emergency response plan after a full or partial
 exercise;
(b) debriefing and analysing the emergency response operations after an emergency situation; and
(c) developing new emergency procedures or systems as part of the emergency response plan when
new hazards are identified by the safety management system, to ensure, amongst others, the
coordination with the emergency response plans of other interfacing organisations.

title: Management system
text:
COMPLIANCE MONITORING
(a) Compliance monitoring
(1) The implementation and use of a compliance monitoring process should enable the
Aerodrome Operator  to monitor compliance with the relevant requirements of CAR AGA, as
well as any other applicable regulatory requirements, or requirements established by the
Aerodrome Operator  and to that effect:
(i) the Aerodrome Operator  should specify the basic structure of the compliance
monitoring applicable to the activities conducted;
(ii) the compliance monitoring should be properly implemented, maintained and
continually reviewed and improved as necessary;
(iii) compliance monitoring should be structured according to the size of organisation and
to include the activities and services for which the Aerodrome Operator  is responsible
as required in CAR AGA,  including those which have been subcontracted;
(iv) compliance monitoring should include a feedback system of findings to the
accountable manager to ensure effective implementation of corrective actions as
necessary.
(2) An Aerodrome Operator  should monitor conformance with the procedures it has designed,
to ensure safe activities. In doing so, an Aerodrome Operator  should as a minimum, and
where appropriate, monitor compliance with:
(i) Applicable CARs;

(ii) Scope of the certificate;
(iii) manuals, logs, and records;
(iv) training standards;
(v) required resources; and
(vi) management system procedures and manuals.
(b) Organisational set-up
(i) A person should be responsible for compliance monitoring. The Accountable Manager, with
regards to his/her direct accountability for safety, should ensure that sufficient resources are
allocated for compliance monitoring.
(ii) The independence of the compliance monitoring should be established by ensuring that
audits and inspections are carried out by personnel not responsible for the function,
procedure, etc. being audited.
(iii) Personnel involved in compliance monitoring should have access to any part of the
aerodrome organisation, and any contracted organisation as required.
 (c) Compliance monitoring documentation
(1) Relevant documentation should include the relevant part(s) of the Aerodrome Operator’s
 management system documentation.
(2) In addition, relevant documentation should also include the following:
(i) terminology;
(ii) SOP(s);
(iii) a description of the organisation of the Aerodrome Operator ;
(iv) the allocation of duties and responsibilities;
(v) procedures to ensure regulatory compliance;
(vi) the compliance monitoring programme, reflecting:
(A) schedule of the monitoring programme;

(B) audit procedures;
(C) reporting procedures;
(D) follow-up and corrective action procedures; and
(E) recording system.
(vii) the training syllabus referred to in (d)(2); and
(viii) document control.
(d) Training
(1) applicable role related  training is essential to optimise compliance .In order to achieve
significant outcomes of such training, the operator should ensure that all personnel
understand the objectives as laid down in the operator’s management system
documentation.
(2) Those responsible for managing the compliance monitoring should receive training on this
task. Such training should cover the requirements of compliance monitoring, manuals and
procedures related to the task, audit techniques, reporting, and recording. Audits should be
carried out by trained auditing personnel who are independent of those having direct
responsibility for the activity being audited.
(3) Time should be provided to train the personnel involved in compliance management, and for
briefing the remaining of the personnel.
(4) The allocation of time and resources should be based on the volume and complexity of the
activities concerned.
(e) Compliance monitoring — audit scheduling
(1) A defined audit schedule to be completed during a specified calendar period and a periodic
review cycle for each area for which the Aerodrome Operator  is responsible should be
established. The programme should allow for unscheduled audits when trends  indicating
safety concerns are identified. Follow -up actions/ reviews/ audits should be scheduled to
verify that corrective action was carried out, and that it was effective and completed.

(2) The aerodrome, its management system key processes, procedures and its operation should
be audited within the first 12 months since the date of the issuance of the certificate.
(3) After that, the Aerodrome Operator  should consider the results of its safety (risk)
assessments and of its past compliance monitoring activities, in order to adapt the calendar
period within which an audit or a series of audits should be conducted, to cover the whole
aerodrome, its managem ent system key processes, procedures and its operation in a
manner, and at intervals as determined by the Aerodrome Operator .
(4) Ensure the results of audits are shared with the personnel responsible for the activity being
audited; and establish and implement a mechanism to escalate to the accountable manager
where necessary.
(5) Required preventive or corrective action to be taken by the personnel responsible for the
activity being audited if findings (or) area of enhancement are found by the audit.
(6) Ensure all audit findings and observations are evidenced and properly recorded.
(7) Management review procedures that should include the use of statistical analysis, to ensure
the continuing suitability and effectiveness of the quality assurance system in satisfying the
requirements of this regulations.

title: Management system
text:
RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE MONITORING
(a) The responsibility for the compliance monitoring should be with the quality Post Holder who has
direct access to, and is responsible to the Accountable Manager.
(b) Persons allocated the responsibility for the compliance monitoring should have:
(1) adequate experience and expertise in aerodrome operations;
(2) adequate knowledge of, and experience in safety management and quality assurance;
(3) knowledge of the aerodrome manual; and
(4) comprehensive knowledge of the applicable requirements of this CAR and associated ICAO
documents.

title: Management system
text:
RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE MONITORING- LAA
(a) In case of LAA, the responsibility for compliance monitoring can be carried out by competent and
suitable person.
(b) In case external personnel are used to perform compliance audits or inspections:
(1) any such audits or inspections are performed under the responsibility of the quality Post
Holder; and
(2) the quality Post Holder remains responsible for ensuring that the external personnel have
relevant knowledge, background and experience as appropriate to the activities being
audited or inspected, including knowledge and experience in compliance monitoring.
 The quality Post Holder retains the ultimate responsibility for the effectiveness of the
compliance monitoring function, in particular for the effective implementation and follow -
up of all corrective actions.

title: Management system
text:
AERODROME OPERATOR MANAGEMENT SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
The Aerodrome Operator  should ensure that the documented management system key processes
include a process for making personnel aware of their responsibilities, as well as its amendment
procedure.
The Aerodrome Operator’s management system documentation should, at least, include the following
information:
(a) a statement signed by the Accountable Manager to confirm that the Aerodrome Operator  will
continuously work in accordance with the applicable requirements and the operator’s
documentation;
(b) the Aerodrome Operator’s scope of activities;
(c) the titles and details of persons  referred to in ADR.OR.A.025 and ADR.OR.A.030 – Personnel
requirements, as applicable;
(d) an organisation chart showing the lines of responsibility between the Post Holders;

(e) procedures specifying how the Aerodrome Operator  ensures compliance with the applicable
requirements;
(f) the amendment procedure for the operator’s management system documentation; and
(g) safety management system outputs.

title: Management system
text:
AERODROME OPERATOR’S SAFETY MANAGEMENT MANUAL
(a) The Safety Management Manual (SMM), should be the key instrument for communicating the
approach to safety for the Aerodrome Operator .
(b) The SMM should document all aspects of safety management, including the safety policy,
objectives, procedures, and individual safety responsibilities.

title: Management system
Management of aeronautical data and aeronautical information
text:
As part of its management system, the Aerodrome Operator  shall implement and maintain a quality
management system covering the following activities:
(1) its aeronautical data activities;
(2) its aeronautical information provision activities.

title: Management of aeronautical data and aeronautical information
text:
QUALITY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM FOR AERONAUTICAL DATA AND AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION
PROVISION ACTIVITIES
(a) An Aerodrome Operator  does not need to duplicate functions and activities in order to discharge
the responsibilities related to the management of aeronautical data and aeronautical information
provision activities.
(b) In this respect, the compliance monitoring may be used for the purposes of ensuring compliance with
the relevant requirements for management of aeronautical data and aeronautical information
provision activities.

title: Management of aeronautical data and aeronautical information
text:
Protection of electronic aeronautical data while stored or in transit should be totally monitored by the
cyclic redundancy check (CRC). To achieve protection of the integrity level of critical and essential
aeronautical data as classified in ADR.OPS.A.010 - Data quality requirements.

title: Management of aeronautical data and aeronautical information
text:
Aerodrome oper ator should have p rocedures to ensure that aeronautical data submitted to the
Aeronautical Information Service as part of the Integrated Aeronautical Information P roduct, is at any
moment:
(a) checked and coordinated with relevant parties before it is submitted to the Aeronautical
Information Service, in order to make certain that all necessary information has been included
and that it is correct in detail;
(b) traceable to its origin to allow any data anomalies or errors, detected during
production/maintenance phases or in operational use, to be corrected; and
(c) validated and verified to ensure that quality requirements (accuracy , resolution, integrity) and
traceability of aeronautical data as specified in this CAR  are met.

title: Training and proficiency check programmes
text: See CAR AGA PART TRG

title: Facilities requirements
text:
(a) The Aerodrome Operator  shall ensure that adequate and appropriate facilities are available to
its personnel or personnel employed by parties with whom it has contracted for the provision of
aerodrome operational and maintenance services.
(b) The Aerodrome Operator  shall designate appropriate areas at the aerodrome to be used for the
storage of dangerous goods transported through the aerodrome, in accordance  with the
relevant Technical Instructions.

title: Coordination with other organisations
text:
The Aerodrome Operator  shall:
(a) ensure that the management system of the aerodrome addresses the coordination and interface
with the safety procedures of other organisations operating or providing services at the aerodrome;
and

(b) ensure that such organisations have safety procedures in place to comply with the applicable
requirements of this CAR and the requirements laid down in the aerodrome manual.

title: Coordination with other organisations
Safety programmes
text:
The Aerodrome Operator  shall:
(a) establish, lead and implement programmes to promote safety and the exchange of safety- relevant
information; and
(b) require organisations operating or providing services at the aerodrome to be involved in such
programmes.

title: Safety programmes
text:
SAFETY PROGRAMMES — AERODROME SAFETY COMMITTEES
(a) The Aerodrome Operator  should:
(1) organise, coordinate and implement programmes to promote safety at the aerodrome.

(2) coordinate and promote the exchange of information, and investigation of occurrences,
serious incidents, and accidents.
(b) The Aerodrome Operator  should establish, coordinate, and lead the local aerodrome safety
committees, and a Local Runway Safety Team, dealing with runway safety, taxiway safety, apron
safety, and the safety of the operations at the aerodrome in general. All relevant organisation s
operating or providing services at the aerodrome should participate  in such aerodrome safety
committees and the Local Runway Safety Team.
 The local aerodrome safety committees and the Local Runway Safety Team should convene
regularly, identify and review local safety issues, and examine possible solutions, and need for
action. Minutes of such meetings should be kept. Terms of Reference relevant to the functioning of
local aerodrome safety committees and the Local Runway Safety Team should be included in the
aerodrome manual.
(c) Proactive measures should be taken by Aerodrome Operator s to reduce the likelihood of a runway
incursion occurring at their aerodrome and to raise awareness of the hazards associated with
runway incursions to all aerodrome users. Aerodrome operators should regularly review those
areas of their aerodrome Safety Management System relevant to the effectiveness and adequacy
of the prevention measures in place at their aerodrome.

title: Safety programmes
Safety programmes
Safety programmes
Safety programmes
text:
HOT SPOTS
Once hot spots have been identified at an aerodrome, suitable strategies should be implemented to
remove the hazard and, when this is not immediately possible, to manage and mitigate the risk, including
the publication of hot spot charts in the Aeronautical Information Publication.

title: Safety programmes
Aerodrome safety reporting system
text:
(a) The Aerodrome Operator  shall establish and implement a safety reporting system for all personnel
and organisations operating or providing services at the aerodrome, in order to promote safety at,
and the safe use of, the aerodrome.
(b) The Aerodrome Operator  shall:
(1) require that the personnel and organisations mentioned in point (a) use the safety reporting
system for the mandatory reporting of any accident, serious incident and occurrence; and
(2) ensure that the safety reporting system be used for the voluntary reporting of any defect,
fault and safety hazard which could impact safety.
(c) The safety reporting system shall protect the identity of the reporter, encourage voluntary
reporting and include the possibility that reports may be submitted anonymously.
(d) The Aerodrome Operator  shall:
(1) record all reports submitted;
(2) analyse and assess the reports, as appropriate, in order to address safety deficiencies and
identify trends;
(3) ensure that all organisations operating or providing services at the aerodrome which are
relevant to the safety concern, participate in the analysis of such reports and that any
corrective and/or preventive measures identified are implemented;
(4) conduct investigations of reports, as appropriate.

title: Safety reporting system
Safety reporting system
text:
NEED FOR SAFETY REPORTING
(a) The overall purpose of the safety reporting system is to use reported information to improve the
level of safety performance of the aerodrome, and not to attribute blame.
(b) The objectives of the safety reporting system should be:
(1) to enable an assessment to be made of the safety implications of each relevant occurrence,
serious incident and accident, including previous similar events, so that any necessary action
can be initiated; and
(2) to ensure that knowledge of relevant occurrences, serious incidents and accidents is
disseminated, so that other persons and organisations may learn from them.

title: Record keeping
Record keeping
text:
GENERAL- DOCUMENTATION TO BE RETAINED
(a) The system employed by the Aerodrome Operator  for record keeping should provide for adequate
procedures, storage facilities, and reliable traceability, retrievability and accessibility of the records
related to the activities of the Aerodrome Operator , throughout the required retention period.
(b) The records should remain legible throughout the required retention period. The retention period
starts when the record has been created or last amended.
(c) Computer systems should include safeguards against the ability of unauthorised personnel to alter
the data.
(d) When hardware or software changes take place, special care should be taken that all necessary
data continues to be accessible, at least, through the full retention period.

title: Record keeping
text:
RECORDING OF AIRCRAFT MOVEMENTS
(a) The Aerodrome Operator  should employ a system to be used for   recording  the  aircraft
movements at the aerodrome.
(b) Such a system should allow the Aerodrome Operator  to record:
(1) the number of movements of each aircraft type using the aerodrome;
(2) the type of each aircraft movement (commercial air transportation, cargo, etc.);
(3) the date of each movement; and

(4) the number of passengers.
(c) The system used should also consider the provisions of GM1 ADR.OR.G.035.

title: Continuing compliance with the Certification Specifications (CS)
text:
The Aerodrome Operator , following an amendment of the Certification Specifications, shall:
(a) perform a review to identify any Certification Specifications which are applicable to the aerodrome;
and
(b) if relevant, initiate a change process in accordance with ADR.OR.H.065-Changes, before
implementing the changes at the aerodrome.

title: Changes
text:
(a) Any change:
(1) affecting the scope of the Aerodrome Certificate/ Landing Area Acceptance, its compliance
register and safety-critical aerodrome equipment; or
(2) significantly affecting elements of the Aerodrome Operator ’s management system as
required in ADR.OR.G.005(b)- Management system;
shall require prior approval by the GCAA.
(b) For changes as mentioned in (a) requiring prior approval, the Aerodrome Operator  shall notify,
apply for and obtain an approval issued by the GCAA.
(c) The application for a change in accordance with point ( b)  shall be submitted before any such
change takes place, in order to enable the GCAA to determine continued compliance with the
requirements of this CAR and to amend, if necessary, the Aerodrome Certificate /Landing Area
Acceptance and related scope and conditions attached to it.
 The change shall only be implemented upon receipt of formal approval by the GCAA.
 During the changes, the Aerodrome Operator  shall operate under the conditions approved by the
GCAA.
(d) The Aerodrome Operator  shall provide the GCAA with the relevant documentation in accordance
with point (e).
(e) As a part of its management system, as defined in ADR.OR.G.005- Management system , the
Aerodrome Operator  proposing a change to the aerodrome, its operation, its organisation or its
management system shall:

(1) determine the interdependencies with any affected parties, plan and conduct a safety
assessment in coordination with these organisations;
(2) align responsibilities, actions and mitigations with any affected parties, in a systematic way;
(3) ensure a comprehensive assessment of the change including any necessary interactions; and
(4) ensure that evidence and safety criteria are established and documented to support the
safety assessment, and that the change supports the improvement of safety whenever
reasonably practicable.
(f) Changes shall be properly coordinated within the organisation, with other service providers, users
of the services, and other relevant undertakings.
(g) Aerodrome operator, while managing a change should comply with the requirements of CAR
SMS.SA.005- Management of Change, as amended/updated.
(h) Upon introducing new aircraft types /  subtypes,  irrespective  of the size and the aerodrome
reference code, th e Aerodrome Operator  shall conduct a compatibility study to assess the
compatability ,as per the procedure established by the Aerodrome Operator  , to ensure safe
aircraft operations.

title: Changes
text:
GENERAL – DOCUMENTS REQUIRED
The Aerodrome Operator  should ensure that prior to initiating any change to the aerodrome or its
operation, an application is submitted to the GCAA. The applicant should provide documentation
containing a description of the proposed change, in which the following are identified:
(a) the scope of the certificate, and/or the elements of the compliance register, and/or the safety -
critical aerodrome equipment and/or Aerodrome Operator’s management system and the parts of
aerodrome manual, which are affected by the change, including relevant appropriate detailed
design drawings;
(b) the Certification Specifications with which the proposed change has been designed to comply with,
including the Certification Specifications for which the applicant proposes to show compliance in a
different manner in order to demonstrate an equivalent level of safety;

(c) the requirements of Subpart ADR.OR and Subpart ADR.OPS, and any other applicable requirements
that have to be complied with as a result of the proposed change, including the way in which
compliance is intended to be demonstrated; and
(d) the safety assessment as required for the proposed change.

title: Changes
text:
CHANGES REQUIRING PRIOR APPROVAL
(a) Use of alternative means of compliance as required by ADR.OR.A.015 (c)- Means of compliance.
(b) Changes   to   the   compliance register , the conditions,  scope   of   the   certificate, as   required
by ADR.OR.H.065(a)(1) Changes.
(c) Changes to safety-critical aerodrome equipment as required by ADR.OR.H.065(a)(1) Changes.
(d) Changes significantly affecting elements of the Aerodrome Operator’s  management system as
required by ADR.OR.H.065(a)(2) Changes.
(e) Changes to the level of protection of rescue and firefighting services as required by PART ACM.
(f) Changes to Post Holders and Accountable Manager as required by ADR.OR.A.025 and ADR.OR.A.30
– Personnel Requirement.
(g) Changes to low-visibility procedures as required by ADR.OPS.B.045.
(h) Use of aerodrome by aircraft exceeding the certified design characteristics of the  aerodrome  as
required by ADR.OPS.B.090.
(i) New aerodrome infrastructure or changes to the existing aerodrome infrastructure in the airside
including but not limiting to visual aids/ navigational facilities, extensions/ reductions to pavement
areas for use by aircraft; the erection of new buildings and alterations to existing buildings.
(j) Major maintenance, including refurbishment of the existing infrastructure.
(k) Reduction in aerodrome infrastructure and the changes to the compliance register, including long
term closures of aerodrome infrastructure for upgrade, downgrade, investigation purpose.
(l) Airfield works that will result in the non-availability of critical aerodrome infrastructure or facility.
(m) Where specifically mentioned in this CAR.

(n) When requested by the GCAA.

title: Changes
text:
GENERAL - CHANGE MANAGEMENT PROCEDURES
Notwithstanding the requirements of CAR SMS,
(a) The Aerodrome Operator’s procedures, should cover the complete lifecycle of a change.
(b) The Aerodrome Operator  should show that the procedures address all the actions and all the
evidence needed in order to comply with the requirements, as appropriate. For this purpose, the
Aerodrome Operator  should use a compliance matrix, which:
(1) identifies applicable regulations;
(2) provides the current status of compliance and the status of compliance following
implementation of the change;
(3) details of measures taken to achieve compliance;
(4) the rationale explaining how the procedures demonstrate compliance with the regulation;
and
(5) The rationale justifying any non -compliance identified along with the proposed mitigations
to demonstrate equivalent level of safety.
(c) The Aerodrome Operator  should include in the procedures:
(1) Accountabilities, roles and responsibilities for the change management processes
 identified in the procedures;
(2) Project timeline (where applicable);
 Including but not limiting to , start date, key milestones, OLS , OPS and other aeronautical
surveys, friction testing, flight calibrations, photometric testing, lux levels, pavement
assessments, AIP publications, operational trials, internal verification and acceptance and the
timescales for GCAA’s review/ inspection and acceptance process;
(3) Interfaces with Safety Management Systems or other required systems; and
(4) Lines of communication or liaison with other involved parties.
