text: An arrangement under which an operator places its designator code on a flight operated by another operator, and sells and issues tickets for that flight.

title: Collision
text: An impact, other than an impact associated with normal operating circumstances, between aircraft, or between an aircraft and another object.

title: Collision avoidance logic
text: The sub-system or part of ACAS that analyses data relating to an intruder and own aircraft, decides whether or not advisories are appropriate and, if so, generates the advisories. It includes the following functions: range and altitude tracking, threat detection and RA generation. It excludes surveillance.

title: COMAT
text: Operator material carried on an operator’s aircraft for the operator’s own purposes.

title: Combined vision system (CVS)
text: A system to display images from a combination of an enhanced vision system (EVS) and a synthetic vision system (SVS).

title: Command and control (C2) link
text: .The data link between the remotely piloted aircraft and the remote pilot station for the purposes of managing the flight.

title: Commander
text: See: Pilot In Command.

title: Commencement of journey
text: The point at which the person began his journey, without taking into account any airport at which he stopped in direct transit, either on a through-flight or a connecting flight, if he did not leave the direct transit area of the airport in question.

title: Commercial air transport flight
text: See: Commercial air transport operation.

title: Commercial air transport operation
text: An aircraft operation involving the transport of passengers, cargo or mail for remuneration or hire. NOTE: The term ‘aircraft operator’ is also used instead of commercial air transport operator.

title: Commissary supplies
text: Items, either disposable or intended for multiple use, that are used by the aircraft operator for provision of services during flights, in particular for catering, and for the comfort of passengers.

title: Common mark
text: A mark assigned by the International Civil Aviation Organization to the common mark registering authority registering aircraft of an international operating agency on other than a national basis. Note.— All aircraft of an international operating agency which are registered on other than a national basis will bear the same common mark.

title: Common mark registering authority
text: The authority maintaining the non-national register or, where appropriate, the part thereof, in which aircraft of an international operating agency are registered.

title: Communication centre
text: An aeronautical fixed station which relays or retransmits telecommunication traffic from (or to) a number of other aeronautical fixed stations directly connected to it.

title: Competency
text: A combination of skills, knowledge and attitudes required to perform a task to the prescribed standard.

title: Competency element
text: An action that constitutes a task that has a triggering event and a terminating event that clearly defines its limits, and an observable outcome.

title: Competency unit
text: A discrete function consisting of a number of competency elements.

title: Competent Authority
text: The General Civil Aviation Authority or any of its departments to which supervision and development of civil aviation affairs is assigned.

title: Complex motor- powered aircraft’
text: Complex motor-powered aircraft shall mean: (i) an aeroplane: — with a maximum certificated take-off mass exceeding 5 700 kg, or — certificated for a maximum passenger seating configuration of more than nineteen, or — certificated for operation with a minimum crew of at least two pilots, or — equipped with (a) turbojet engine(s) or more than one turboprop engine, or (ii) a helicopter certificated: — for a maximum take-off mass exceeding 3 175 kg, or — for a maximum passenger seating configuration of more than nine, or — for operation with a minimum crew of at least two pilots, or (iii) a tilt rotor aircraft;

title: Component
text: Any engine, propeller, part or appliance.

title: Computer
text: A device which performs sequences of arithmetical and logical steps upon data AN6/III, without human intervention.

title: Conditional Clearance
text: An ATC clearance issued to an aircraft which does not become effective until a specified condition has been satisfied. The condition will normally relate to another aircraft or vehicle.

title: Conference communications
text: Communication facilities whereby direct speech conversation may be conducted between three or more locations simultaneously.

title: Confidence level
text: The probability that the true value of a parameter is within a certain interval around the estimate of its value. Note.— The interval is usually referred to as the accuracy of the estimate.

title: Configuration (as applied to the aeroplane)
text: A particular combination of the positions of the moveable elements, such as wing flaps and landing gear, etc., that affects the aerodynamic characteristics of the aeroplane.

title: Configuration Deviation List (CDL)
text: A list established by the organisation responsible for the type design with the approval of the State of Design which identifies any external parts of an aircraft type which may be missing at the commencement of a flight, and which contains, where necessary, any information on associated operating limitations and performance correction.

title: Congested area
text: In relation to a city, town or settlement, any area which is substantially used for residential, commercial or recreational purposes.

title: Congested hostile environment
text: A hostile environment within a congested area.

title: Consent
text: An electronic consent to a registration with the International Registry.

title: Consignment
text: One or more packages accepted by an operator from one shipper at one time and at one address, receipted for in one lot and moving to one consignee at one destination address.

title: Consultation
text: Discussion with a meteorologist or another qualified person of existing and/or expected meteorological conditions relating to flight operations; a discussion includes answers to questions

title: C ontaminated runway
text: A runway of which more than 25% of the runway surface area within the required length and width being used is covered by the following: a) surface water more than 3 mm (0.125 in) deep, or by slush, or loose snow, equivalent to more than 3 mm (0.125 in) of water; b) snow which has been compressed into a solid mass which resists further compression and will hold together or break into lumps if picked up (compacted snow); or c) ice, including wet ice.

title: Contaminated runway
text: A runway is contaminated when a significant portion of the runway surface area (whether in isolated areas or not) within the length and width being used is covered by one or more of the substances listed in the runway surface condition descriptors. AN6 Note.— Further information on runway surface condition descriptors can be found in the Annex 14, Volume I — Definitions.

title: Contingency fuel
text: The fuel required to compensate for unforeseen factors that could have an influence on the fuel consumption to the destination aerodrome.

title: Contingency Plan
text: A proactive plan to include measures and procedures addressing various threat levels, risk assessments and the associated security measures to be implemented; designed to anticipate and mitigate events as well as prepare all concerned parties having roles and responsibilities in the event of an actual act of unlawful interference. A contingency plan sets forth incremental security measures that may be elevated as the threat increases. It may be a stand-alone plan or included as part of a Crisis Management Plan.

title: Continued Airworthiness Management Exposition (CAME)
text: A document approved by the authority. It contains procedures specifying how the continuing airworthiness management organisation ensures compliance with airworthiness requirements.

title: Continued Airworthiness Management Organisation (CAMO)
text: An organisation approved by the authority to: Manage all of the processes ensuring that, at any time in its operating life, the aircraft complies with the airworthiness requirements in force and is in a condition for safe operation.

title: Continuing airworthiness
text: The set of processes by which an aircraft, engine, propeller or part complies with the applicable airworthiness requirements and remains in a condition for safe operation throughout its operating life. AN6/III,

title: Continuing airworthiness records
text: Records which are related to the continuing airworthiness status of an aircraft, engine, propeller or associated part.

title: Continuous Descent Final Approach (CDFA)
text: A technique, consistent with stabilised approach procedures, for flying the final- approach segment of a non-precision instrument approach procedure as a continuous descent, without level-off, from an altitude/height at or above the final approach fix altitude/height to a point approximately 15 m (50 ft) above the landing runway threshold or the point where the flare manoeuvre shall begin for the type of aircraft flown.

title: Contour line
text: A line on a map or chart connecting points of equal elevation.

title: Contract of Sale
text: A contract for the sale of an object by a seller to a buyer which is different than a security agreement, a title reservation agreement or a leasing agreement.

title: Contracting State
text: A State that is a signatory to the Convention on International Civil Aviation.

title: Contributing factors
text: Actions, omissions, events, conditions, or a combination thereof, which, if eliminated or avoided, would have reduced the probability of the accident or incident occurring, or mitigated the severity of the consequences of the accident or incident. The identification of contributing factors does not imply the assignment of fault or the determination of administrative, civil or criminal liability.

title: Control Area (CTA)
text: A controlled airspace extending upwards from a specified limit above the earth.

title: Control tower
text: See: Aerodrome control tower.

title: Control zone (CTR)
text: A controlled airspace extending upwards from the surface of the earth to a specified upper limit.

title: Controlled aerodrome
text: An aerodrome at which air traffic control service is provided to aerodrome traffic. Note.— The term “controlled aerodrome” indicates that air traffic control service is provided to aerodrome traffic but does not necessarily imply that a control zone exists.

title: Controlled airspace
text: An airspace of defined dimensions within which air traffic control service is provided in accordance with the airspace classification. NOTE: [PANS-OPS/I]: Controlled airspace is a generic term which covers ATS airspace Classes A, B, C, D and E as described in 2.6 of Annex 11.

title: Controlled flight
text: , Any flight which is subject to an air traffic control clearance.

title: Controller-Pilot Data Link Communications (CPDLC)
text: A means of communication between controller and pilot, using data link for ATC communications. AN11,

extra.icao_source: AN2, AN11, ATM AN10/II, AN10/III, AN15, ATM

title: Conversion process
text: A type of technology used to convert a feedstock into aviation fuel.

title: Converted Meteorological visibility (CMV)
text: A value, equivalent to an RVR, which is derived from the reported meteorological visibility.

title: Co-pilot
text: A licensed pilot serving in any piloting capacity other than as pilot-in-command but excluding a pilot who is on board the aircraft for the sole purpose of receiving flight instruction.

title: Corporate aviation/ business aviation
text: The non-commercial operation or use of aircraft by a company for the carriage of passengers or goods as an aid to the conduct of company business, flown by a professional pilot employed to fly the aircraft. NOTE: Corporate aviation is a subset of general aviation.

title: CORSIA eligible fuel
text: A CORSIA sustainable aviation fuel or a CORSIA lower carbon aviation fuel, which an operator may use to reduce their offsetting requirements.

title: CORSIA lower carbon aviation fuel
text: A fossil-based aviation fuel that meets the CORSIA Sustainability Criteria under Volume IV of Annex 16.

title: CORSIA sustainable aviation fuel
text: A renewable or waste-derived aviation fuel that meets the CORSIA Sustainability Criteria under Volume IV of Annex 16.

title: Corporate aviation operation
text: The non-commercial operation or use of aircraft by a company for the carriage of passengers or goods as an aid to the conduct of company business, flown by a professional pilot(s) employed to fly the aircraft.

title: COSPAS-SARSAT System
text: A satellite and ground station network that is designed to detect electronic distress beacons and to provide accurate, timely and reliable distress alert and location data to help search and rescue authorities assist persons in distress.

title: Coulomb (c)
text: The quantity of electricity transported in 1 second by a current of 1 ampere.

title: CPDLC message
text: Information exchanged between an airborne system and its ground counterpart. A CPDLC message consists of a single message element or a combination of message elements conveyed in a single transmission by the initiator.

title: CPDLC message set
text: A list of standard message elements and free text message elements.

title: Craft
text: Any air or sea-surface vehicle, or submersible of any kind or size

title: Credit
text: Recognition of alternative means or prior qualifications.

title: Crew member
text: COMMISSION REGULATION a person assigned by an operator to perform duties on board an aircraft air

title: Crew member
text: A person assigned by an operator to duty on an aircraft during a flight AN6/III, duty period.

title: Critical engine(s)
text: See: Critical power-unit(s). Any engine whose failure gives the most adverse effect on the aircraft characteristics relative to the case under consideration. Note: On some aircraft there may be more than one equally critical engine. In this case, the expression “the critical engine” means one of those critical engines.

title: Critical Part
text: Where the failure analysis shows that a part must achieve and maintain a particularly high level of integrity if Hazardous Effects are not to occur at a rate in excess of Extremely Remote then such a part shall be identified as a Critical Part.

title: Critical phases of flight (Aeroplane)
text: The take-off run, the take-off flight path, the final approach, the missed approach, the landing, including the landing roll, and any other phases of flight as determined by the pilot-in-command or commander.

title: Critical phases of flight (helicopters)
text: Taxiing, hovering, take-off, final approach, missed approach, the landing and any other phases of flight as determined by the pilot-in-command or commander.

title: Critical power-unit(s) / critical engine(s)
text: The power-unit(s) failure of which gives the most adverse effect on the aircraft characteristics relative to the case under consideration.

title: Cross-country
text: A flight between a point of departure and a point of arrival following a pre- planned route using standard navigation procedures.

title: Cross-country flight
text: See: Cross-country.

title: Cruise climb / drift up
text: An aeroplane cruising technique resulting in a net increase in altitude as the aeroplane mass decreases.

title: Cruise relief pilot
text: A flight crew member who is assigned to perform pilot tasks during cruise flight, to allow the pilot-in-command or a co-pilot to obtain planned rest.

title: Cruising level
text: A level maintained during a significant portion of a flight. AN6/I,

title: Culture
text: All man-made features constructed on the surface of the Earth, such as cities, railways and canals.

title: Current Data Authority (CDA)
text: The designated ground system through which a CPDLC dialogue between a pilot AN10/II, and a controller currently responsible for the flight is permitted to take place.

title: Current flight Plan (CPL)
text: The flight plan, including changes, if any, brought about by subsequent clearances.

title: Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC)
text: A mathematical algorithm applied to the digital expression of data that provides a level of assurance against loss or alteration of data.

title: Damp runway
text: A runway where the surface is not dry, but when the moisture on it does not give it a shiny appearance.

title: Danger area (D)
text: An airspace of defined dimensions within which activities dangerous to the flight of aircraft may exist at specified times.

title: Dangerous goods
text: Articles or substances which are capable of posing a risk to health, safety, property or the environment and which are shown in the list of dangerous goods in the Technical Instructions or which are classified according to those Instructions.

title: Dangerous goods accident
text: An occurrence associated with and related to the transport of dangerous goods by air which results in fatal or serious injury to a person or major property damage.

title: Dangerous goods incident
text: An occurrence, other than a dangerous goods accident, associated with and related to the transport of dangerous goods by air, not necessarily occurring on board an aircraft, which results in injury to a person, property damage, fire, breakage, spillage, leakage of fluid or radiation or other evidence that the integrity of the packaging has not been maintained. Any occurrence relating to the transport of dangerous goods which seriously jeopardizes the aircraft or its occupants is also deemed to constitute a dangerous goods incident.

title: Data Accuracy
text: See: System accuracy. A degree of conformance between the estimated or measured value and the AN14/I, true value.

title: Data completeness
text: The degree of confidence that all of the data needed to support the intended use is provided.

title: Data convention
text: An agreed set of rules governing the manner or sequence in which a set of data may be combined into a meaningful communication.

title: Data format
text: A structure of data elements, records and files arranged to meet standards, specifications or data quality requirements.

title: Data integrity (assurance level)
text: A degree of assurance that an aeronautical data and its value has not been lost or altered since the origination or authorized amendment. AN14/I,

title: Data link-Automatic Terminal Information Service (D-ATIS)
text: The provision of ATIS via data link. AN11,

title: Data link communications
text: A form of communication intended for the exchange of messages via a data link.

title: Data link flight information services (D-FIS)
text: The provision of FIS via data link.

title: Data Link Initiation Capability (DLIC)
text: A data link application that provides the ability to exchange addresses, names and version numbers necessary to initiate data link applications.

title: Data processing
text: A systematic sequence of operations performed on data.

title: Data product
text: Data set or data set series that conforms to a data product specification (ISO 19131*). ISO Standard 19131, Geographic information; Data product specification

title: Data product specification
text: Detailed description of a data set or data set series together with additional information that will enable it to be created, supplied to and used by another party (ISO 19131*). Note.— A data product specification provides a description of the universe of discourse and a specification for mapping the universe of discourse to a data set. It may be used for production, sales, end-use or other purpose. ISO Standard 19131, Geographic information; Data product specification

title: Data quality
text: A degree or level of confidence that the data provided meet the requirements of the data user in terms of accuracy, resolution and integrity (or equivalent assurance level), traceability, timeliness, completeness and format.

title: Data resolution
text: A number of units or digits to which a measured or calculated value is expressed and used.

title: Data set
text: Identifiable collection of data (ISO 19101*).

title: Data set series
text: Collection of data sets sharing the same product specification (ISO 19115*). *ISO Standard 19115, Geographic information; Metadata.

title: Data timeliness
text: The degree of confidence that the data is applicable to the period of its intended use.

title: Data traceability
text: The degree that a system or a data product can provide a record of the changes made to that product and thereby enable an audit trail to be followed from the end-user to the originator.

title: Database (DB)
text: One or more files of data so structured that appropriate applications may draw from the files and update them.

title: Date of manufacture
text: The date of issue of the document attesting that the individual aircraft or engine as appropriate conforms to the requirements of the type or the date of an analogous document.

title: Datum
text: Any quantity or set of quantities that may serve as a reference or basis for the calculation of other quantities (ISO 19104*). *ISO Standard 19104, Geographic information; Terminology.

title: Deadheading crew
text: A crew member positioned by the operator in flight or by surface transport.

title: Decision altitude (DA) or decision height (DH)
text: A specified altitude or height, in the precision approach or approach with vertical guidance at which a missed approach must be initiated if the required visual reference to continue the approach has not been established. NOTE 1: Decision altitude (DA) is referenced to mean sea level and decision height (DH) is referenced to the threshold elevation. NOTE 2: The required visual reference means that section of the visual aids or of the approach area which should have been in view for sufficient time for the pilot to have made an assessment of the aircraft position and rate of change of position, in relation to the desired flight path. In Category In operations with a decision height the required visual reference is that specified for the particular procedure and operation. NOTE 3: For convenience where both expressions are used they may be written in the form "decision altitude/height" and abbreviated "DA/H"

title: Declarant
text: Any person who makes a goods declaration or in whose name such a declaration is made.

title: Declared capacity
text: A measure of the ability of the ATC system or any of its subsystems or operating positions to provide service to aircraft during normal activities. It is expressed as the number of aircraft entering a specified portion of airspace in a given period of time, taking due account of weather, ATC unit configuration, staff and equipment available, and any other factors that may affect the workload of the controller responsible for the airspace.

title: Declared distances
text: a) Take-Off Run Available (TORA). The length of runway declared available and suitable for the ground run of an aeroplane taking off. b) Take-Off Distance Available (TODA). The length of the take-off run available plus the length of the clearway, if provided. c) Accelerate-Stop Distance Available (ASDA). The length of the take-off run available plus the length of the stopway, if provided. d) Landing Distance Available (LDA). The length of runway which is declared available and suitable for the ground run of an aeroplane landing. NOTE: The calculation of declared distances is described in Annex 14, Volume I, Attachment A.

title: Declared distances - heliports
text: a) Take-Off Distance Available (TODAH). The length of the final approach and take-off area plus the length of helicopter clearway (if provided) declared available and suitable for helicopters to complete the take-off. b) Rejected Take-Off Distance Available (RTODAH). The length of the final approach and take-off area declared available and suitable for performance class 1 helicopters to complete a rejected take-off. c) Landing Distance Available (LDAH). The length of the final approach and take-off area plus any additional area declared available and suitable for helicopters to complete the landing manoeuvre from a defined height.

title: Declared temperature
text: A temperature selected in such a way that when used for performance purposes, over a series of operations, the average level of safety is not less than would be obtained by using official forecast temperatures.

title: Defined Point After Take-Off (DPATO)
text: The point, within the take-off and initial climb phase, before which the helicopter's ability to continue the flight safely, with the critical engine inoperative, is not assured and a forced landing may be required. Note.— Defined points apply to helicopters operating in performance Class 2 only.

title: Defined Point Before Landing (DPBL)
text: The point within the approach and landing phase, after which the helicopter's ability to continue the flight safely, with the critical engine inoperative, is not assured and a forced landing may be required. Note.— Defined points apply to helicopters operating in performance Class 2 only.

title: Degree Celsius (°C)
text: The special name for the unit kelvin for use in stating values of Celsius temperature.

title: De-icing
text: In the case of ground procedures, means a procedure by which frost, ice, snow or slush is removed from an aircraft in order to provide uncontaminated surfaces.

title: De-identification
text: Means removing, from occurrence reports submitted, all personal details pertaining to the reporter and technical details which are leading to the identity of the reporter, or of third parties, being inferred from the information.

title: Dependent parallel approaches
text: Simultaneous approaches to parallel or near-parallel instrument runways where AN14/I, radar separation minima between aircraft on adjacent extended runway centre OPS/I, lines are prescribed.

title: Deportation order
text: A written order, issued by the competent authorities of a State and served upon a deportee, directing him to leave that State.

title: Deportee
text: A person who had legally been admitted to a State by its authorities or who had entered a State illegally, and who at some later time is formally ordered by the competent authorities to leave that State.

title: De-Registration of the aircraft
text: Deletion or removal of the registration of the aircraft from its aircraft register in accordance with the Chicago Convention.

title: Derivative version
text: An aircraft gas turbine engine of the same generic family as an originally type- certificated engine and having features which retain the basic core engine and combustor design of the original model and for which other factors, as judged by the certificating authority, have not changed. Note: Attention is drawn to the difference between the definition of “derived version of an aeroplane” in Volume I of Annex 16 and the definition of “derivative version” in Volume II of Annex 16.

title: Derived version of a helicopter
text: A helicopter which, from the point of view of airworthiness, is similar to the noise certificated prototype but incorporates changes in type design which may affect its noise characteristics adversely. NOTE 1: In applying the Standards of this Annex, a helicopter that is based on an existing prototype but which is considered by the certificating authority to be a new type design for airworthiness purposes shall nevertheless be considered as a derived version if the noise source characteristics are judged by the certificating authority to be the same as the prototype. NOTE 2: “Adversely” refers to an increase of more than 0.30 EPNdB in any one of the noise certification levels for helicopters certificated according to Chapter 8 and 0.30 dB(A) in the certification level for helicopters certificated according to Chapter 11.

title: Derived version of an aeroplane
text: An aeroplane which, from the point of view of airworthiness, is similar to the noise certificated prototype but incorporates changes in type design which may affect its noise characteristics adversely. NOTE 1: Where the certificating authority finds that the proposed change in design, configuration, power or mass is so extensive that a substantially new investigation of compliance with the applicable airworthiness regulations is required, the aeroplane should be considered to be a new type of design rather than a derived version. NOTE 2: “Adversely” refers to an increase of more than 0.10 dB in any one of the noise certification levels unless the cumulative effects of changes in type design are tracked by an approved procedure in which case “adversely” refers to a cumulative increase in the noise level in any one of the noise certification levels of more than 0.30 dB or the margin of compliance, whichever is smaller.

id: CAR-DEF|Derived version of a CO -certified 2 aeroplane
article_no: Derived version of a CO -certified 2 aeroplane
title: Derived version of a CO -certified 2 aeroplane
text: An aeroplane which incorporates changes in type design that either increase its maximum take-off mass, or that increase its CO emissions evaluation metric 2 value by more than: a) 1.35 per cent at a maximum take-off mass of 5 700 kg, decreasing linearly to; b) 0.75 per cent at a maximum take-off mass of 60 000 kg, decreasing linearly to; c) 0.70 per cent at a maximum take-off mass of 600 000 kg; and d) a constant 0.70 per cent at maximum take-off masses greater than 600 000 kg. Note.— Where the certificating authority finds that the proposed change in design, configuration, power or mass is so extensive that a substantially new investigation of compliance with the applicable airworthiness regulations is required, the aeroplane will be considered to be a new type design rather than a derived version.

id: CAR-DEF|Derived version of a non-CO -certified 2 aeroplane
article_no: Derived version of a non-CO -certified 2 aeroplane
title: Derived version of a non-CO -certified 2 aeroplane
text: An individual aeroplane that conforms to an existing Type Certificate, but which is not certified to Annex 16, Volume III, and to which changes in type design are made prior to the issuance of the aeroplane’s first certificate of airworthiness that increase its CO emissions evaluation metric value by more than 1.5 per 2 cent or are considered to be significant CO changes. 2 The maximum mass of the aircraft at which, for structural design purposes, it is assumed that it will be planned to land.

title: Design take-off mass
text: The maximum mass at which the aircraft, for structural design purposes, is assumed to be planned to be at the start of the take-off run.

title: Design taxiing mass
text: The maximum mass of the aircraft at which structural provision is made for load liable to occur during use of the aircraft on the ground prior to the start of take- off.

title: Designated postal operator
text: Any governmental or non-governmental entity officially designated by a Universal Postal Union (UPU) member country to operate postal services and to fulfil the related obligations arising from the acts of the UPU Convention on its territory.

title: Destination alternate
text: An alternate aerodrome to which an aircraft may proceed should it become either impossible or inadvisable to land at the aerodrome of intended landing. AN6/II,

title: Detect and avoid
text: The capability to see, sense or detect conflicting traffic or other hazards and take the appropriate action.

title: DETRESFA
text: The code word used to designate a distress phase.

id: CAR-DEF|Digital Elevation Model (DEM) / Digital Terrain Model (DTM)
article_no: Digital Elevation Model (DEM) / Digital Terrain Model (DTM)
title: Digital Elevation Model (DEM) / Digital Terrain Model (DTM)
text: The representation of terrain surface by continuous elevation values at all intersections of a defined grid, referenced to common datum.

title: Diplomatic Baggage/Pouch
text: A shipping container having diplomatic immunity from search or seizure when accompanied by the required official documentation.

title: Direct transit area
text: A special area established in an international airport, approved by the public authorities concerned and under their direct supervision or control, where passengers can stay during transit or transfer without applying for entry to that State.

title: Direct transit arrangements
text: Special arrangements approved by the public authorities concerned by which traffic which is pausing briefly in its passage through the Contracting State may remain under their direct control.

title: Disabled person
text: See: Person with disabilities.

title: Discrete code
text: A four-digit SSR Code with the last two digits not being ‘00’.

title: Discrete source damage
text: Structural damage of the aeroplane that is likely to result from: impact with a bird, uncontained fan blade failure, uncontained engine failure, uncontained high energy rotating machinery failure or similar causes.

title: Disembarkation
text: The leaving of an aircraft after a landing, except by crew or passengers continuing on the next stage of the same through-flight.

title: Disinfection
text: The procedure whereby health measures are taken to control or kill infectious agents on a human or animal body, in or on affected parts of aircraft, baggage, cargo, goods or containers, as required, by direct exposure to chemical or physical agents.

title: Disinsection
text: The procedure whereby health measures are taken to control or kill insects present in aircraft, baggage, cargo, containers, goods and mail.

title: Displaced Threshold (DTHR)
text: Displaced runway threshold A threshold not located at the extremity of a AN4, runway.

title: Disruptive passenger
text: A passenger who fails to respect the rules of conduct at an airport or on board an aircraft or to follow the instructions of the airport staff or crew members and thereby disturbs the good order and discipline at an airport or on board the aircraft.

title: Distance DR
text: Is the horizontal distance that the helicopter has travelled from the end of the take-off distance available.

title: Distress Phase (DETRESFA)
text: A situation wherein there is a reasonable certainty that an aircraft and its AN11, occupants are threatened by grave and imminent danger and require immediate assistance.

title: Ditching
text: The forced landing of an aircraft on water.

title: Doppler shift
text: The frequency shift observed at a receiver due to any relative motion between transmitter and receiver.

title: Double channel simplex
text: Simplex using two frequency channels, one in each direction. Note.— This method was sometimes referred to as cross-band

title: Downstream clearance
text: A clearance issued to an aircraft by an air traffic control unit that is not the current controlling authority of that aircraft.

title: Dry lease agreement
text: An agreement between undertakings pursuant to which the aircraft is operated under the air operator certificate (AOC) of the lessee.

title: Dry operating mass
text: The total mass of the aircraft ready for a specific type of operation, excluding usable fuel and traffic load.

title: Dry runway
text: A runway is considered dry if its surface is free of visible moisture and not contaminated within the area intended to be used.

id: CAR-DEF|Dual instruction time Applicable until 2 November 2022
article_no: Dual instruction time Applicable until 2 November 2022
title: Dual instruction time Applicable until 2 November 2022
text: Flight time during which a person is receiving flight instruction from a properly authorised pilot on board the aircraft.

id: CAR-DEF|Dual instruction time Applicable as of 3 November 2022
article_no: Dual instruction time Applicable as of 3 November 2022
title: Dual instruction time Applicable as of 3 November 2022
text: Flight time during which a person is receiving flight instruction from a properly authorized pilot on board the aircraft.

title: Duplex
text: A method in which telecommunication between two stations can take place in both directions simultaneously.

title: Duty
text: Any task that flight or cabin crew members are required by the operator to perform, including, for example, flight duty, administrative work, training, positioning and standby when it is likely to induce fatigue.

title: Duty Applicable 5 November 2020
text: Any task that an air traffic controller is required by an air traffic services provider to perform. These tasks include those performed during time-in-position, administrative work and training.

title: Duty period
text: A period which starts when flight crew or cabin crew members are required by an Operator to report for or to commence a duty and ends when that person is free from all duties.

title: Duty period Applicable 5 November 2020
text: A period which starts when an air traffic controller is required by an air traffic services provider to report for or to commence a duty and ends when that person is free from all duties.

title: Dynamic load-bearing surface
text: A surface capable of supporting the loads generated by a helicopter conducting an emergency touchdown on it.

title: Early ETOPS
text: ETOPS type design approval obtained without gaining non-ETOPS service experience on the candidate airplane-engine combination certified for ETOPS.

title: EDTO critical fuel
text: The fuel quantity necessary to fly to an en-route alternate aerodrome considering, at the most critical point on the route, the most limiting system failure.

title: EDTO-significant system
text: An aeroplane system whose failure or degradation could adversely affect the safety particular to an EDTO flight, or whose continued functioning is specifically important to the safe flight and landing of an aeroplane during an EDTO diversion.

title: Effective acceptance bandwidth
text: The range of frequencies with respect to the assigned frequency for which reception is assured when all receiver tolerances have been taken into account.

title: Effective adjacent channel rejection
text: The rejection that is obtained at the appropriate adjacent channel frequency when all relevant receiver tolerances have been taken into account.

title: Effective intensity
text: The effective intensity of a flashing light is equal to the intensity of a fixed light of the same colour which will produce the same visual range under identical conditions of observation.

title: Electronic aeronautical chart display
text: An electronic device by which flight crews are enabled to execute, in a convenient and timely manner, route planning, route monitoring and navigation by displaying required information.

title: Electronic flight bag (EFB)
text: An electronic information system, comprised of equipment and applications for flight crew, which allows for the storing, updating, displaying and processing of EFB functions to support flight operations or duties.

title: Electronic Travel Systems (ETS)
text: The automated process for the lodgement, acceptance and verification of a passenger’s authorization to travel to a State, in lieu of the standard counterfoil paper visa.

id: CAR-DEF|Elevated Final Approach and Take- Off area (elevated FATO)
article_no: Elevated Final Approach and Take- Off area (elevated FATO)
title: Elevated Final Approach and Take- Off area (elevated FATO)
text: Means a FATO that is at least 3 m above the surrounding surface.

title: Elevated heliport
text: A heliport located on a raised structure on land.

title: Elevation (ELEV)
text: Gravity-related height: The vertical distance of a point or a level, on or affixed to AN10/I, the surface of the earth, measured from mean sea level. OPS/I, AN4, The height related to the reference ellipsoid, measured along the ellipsoidal outer normal through the point in question.

extra.icao_source: AN6/III, AN14/II AN3, AN4, ATM, OPS/II AN14/I, AN14/II, AN15

title: Embarkation
text: The boarding of an aircraft for the purpose of commencing a flight, except by such crew or passengers as have embarked on a previous stage of the same through-flight.

title: Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT)
text: A generic term describing equipment which broadcast distinctive signals on designated frequencies and, depending on application, may be automatically activated by impact or be manually activated. AN ELT may be any of the following: Automatic Fixed ELT (ELT(AF)). An automatically activated ELT which is permanently attached to an aircraft. Automatic Portable ELT (ELT(AP)). An automatically activated ELT which is rigidly attached to an aircraft but readily removable from the aircraft. Automatic Deployable ELT (ELT(AD)). An ELT which is rigidly attached to an aircraft and which is automatically deployed and activated by impact, and, in some cases, also byHydrostatic sensors. Manual deployment is also provided. Survival ELT (ELT(S)). An ELT which is removable from an aircraft, stowed so as to facilitate its ready use in an emergency, and manually activated by survivors.

title: Emergency phase
text: A generic term meaning, as the case may be, uncertainty phase, alert phase or , distress phase.

title: Emergency Plan
text: A plan setting forth the procedures for coordinating the response of different aerodrome agencies or services and of those agencies in the surrounding community that could be of assistance in responding to an emergency.

title: eMRTD
text: An MRTD (passport, visa or card) that has a contactless integrated circuit embedded in it and the capability of being used for biometric identification of the MRTD holder in accordance with the standards specified in the relevant Part of Doc 9303 — Machine Readable Travel Documents.

title: End-to-end
text: Pertaining or relating to an entire communication path, typically from (1) the interface between the information source and the communication system at the transmitting end to (2) the interface between the communication system and the information user or processor or application at the receiving end.

title: End-user
text: An ultimate source and/or consumer of information.

id: CAR-DEF|Energy per symbol to noise density ratio (E /N ) s o
article_no: Energy per symbol to noise density ratio (E /N ) s o
title: Energy per symbol to noise density ratio (E /N ) s o
text: The ratio of the average energy transmitted per channel symbol to the average noise power in a 1 Hz bandwidth, usually expressed in dB. For A- BPSK and A-QPSK, one channel symbol refers to one channel bit.

title: Engine (ENG)
text: A unit used or intended to be used for aircraft propulsion. It consists of at least those components and equipment necessary for the functioning and control, but excludes the propeller (if applicable). AN6/III,

title: Enhanced Flight Visibility (EFV)
text: The average forward horizontal distance, from the cockpit of an aircraft in flight, at which prominent topographical objects may be clearly distinguished and identified by day or night by a pilot using an enhanced flight vision system.

title: Enhanced Flight Vision System (EFVS)
text: an installed aircraft system which uses an electronic means to provide a display of the forward external scene topography (the natural or manmade features of a place or region especially in a way to show their relative positions and elevation) through the use of imaging sensors, including but not limited to forward-looking infrared, millimeter wave radiometry, millimeter wave radar, or low-light level image intensification. An EFVS includes the display element, sensors, computers and power supplies, indications, and controls.

title: Enhanced vision system (EVS)
text: A system to display electronic real-time images of the external scene achieved through the use of imaging sensors. Note.— EVS does not include night vision imaging systems (NVIS).

title: En-route alternate
text: An aerodrome at which an aircraft would be able to land after experiencing an abnormal or emergency condition while en route. AN6/II,

title: En-route phase
text: That part of the flight from the end of the take-off and initial climb phase to the commencement of the approach and landing phase.

title: Equivalent airspeed
text: The calibrated airspeed of an aircraft corrected for adiabatic compressible flow for the particular altitude. Equivalent airspeed is equal to calibrated airspeed in standard atmosphere at sea level.

title: Equivalent isotropically radiated power (e.i.r.p.)
text: The product of the power supplied to the antenna and the antenna gain in a given direction relative to an isotropic antenna (absolute or isotropic gain).

title: Equivalent procedure
text: A test or analysis procedure which, while differing from the one specified in this volume of Annex 16, in the technical judgement of the certificating authority yields effectively the same CO emissions evaluation metric value as the 2 specified procedure.

title: Error
text: An action or inaction by an operational person that leads to deviations from organisational or the operational person’s intentions or expectations. Note.— See Chapter 1 of Annex 19 — Safety Management for a definition of operational personnel.

title: Error management
text: The process of detecting and responding to errors with countermeasures that reduce or eliminate the consequences of errors and mitigate the probability of further errors or undesired states. NOTE: See Attachment C to Chapter 3 of the Procedures for Air Navigation Services - Training (PANS-TRG, Doc 9868) and Circular 314 - Threat and Error Management (TEM) in Air Traffic Control for a description of undesired states.

title: Escort
text: An individual authorized by a Contracting State or an aircraft operator to accompany inadmissible persons or deportees being removed from that Contracting State.

title: Essential radio navigation service
text: A radio navigation service whose disruption has a significant impact on operations in the affected airspace or aerodrome.

title: Essential Traffic
text: Essential traffic is that controlled traffic to which the provision of separation by ATC is applicable, but which, in relation to a particular controlled flight is not, or will not be, separated from other controlled traffic by the appropriate separation minimum.

title: Estimated Elapsed Time (EET)
text: The estimated time required to proceed from one significant point to another.

title: Estimated Off-Block Time (EOBT)
text: The estimated time at which the aircraft will commence movement associated with departure.

title: Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA)
text: Estimating arrival for IFR flights, the time at which it is estimated that the aircraft will arrive over that designated point, defined by reference to navigation aids, from which it is intended that an instrument approach procedure will be commenced, or, if no navigation aid is associated with the aerodrome, the time at which the aircraft will arrive over the aerodrome. For VFR flights, the time at which it is estimated that the aircraft will arrive over the aerodrome.

title: Estimating arrival
text: See: Estimated Time of Arrival.

title: Exception
text: A provision in Annex 18 which excludes a specific item of dangerous goods from the requirements normally applicable to that item.

title: Exemption
text: An authorisation issued by an appropriate national authority providing relief from the provisions of Annex 18.

title: Exhaust nozzle
text: In the exhaust emissions sampling of gas turbine engines here the jet effluxes are not mixed (as in some turbofan engines for example) the nozzle considered is that for the gas generator (core) flow only. Where, however, the jet efflux is mixed the nozzle considered is the total exit nozzle.

title: Expected
text: Used in relation to various aspects of performance (e.g. Rate or gradient of climb), this term means the standard performance for the type, in the relevant conditions (e.g. Mass, altitude and temperature).

title: Expected Approach Time (EAT)
text: The time at which ATC expects that an arriving aircraft, following a delay, will leave the holding fix to complete its approach for a landing. Note.— The actual time of leaving the holding fix will depend upon the approach clearance.

title: Explosive Detection System (EDS)
text: A technology system or combination of different technologies which has the ability to detect, and so to indicate by means of an alarm, explosive material contained in baggage or other articles, irrespective of the material from which the bag is made.

title: Explosive Device Detection System (EDDS)
text: A technology system or combination of different technologies which has the ability to detect, and so to indicate by means of an alarm, an explosive device by detecting one or more components of such a device contained in baggage or other articles, irrespective of the material from which the bag or article is made.

title: Explosive substance
text: A solid or liquid substance (or a mixture of substances) which is in itself capable, by chemical reaction, of producing gas at such a temperature and pressure and at such a speed as to cause damage to the surroundings. Included are pyrotechnic substances even when they do not evolve gases. A substance which is not itself an explosive but which can form an explosive atmosphere of gas, vapour or dust is not included.

title: Extended flight over water
text: A flight operated over water at a distance of more than 93 km (50 NM), or 30 minutes at normal cruising speed, whichever is the lesser, away from land suitable for making an emergency landing.

title: Extended range operation
text: Any flight by an aeroplane with two turbine engines where the flight time at the one engine inoperative cruise speed (in ISA and still air conditions), from a point on the route to an adequate alternate aerodrome, is greater than the threshold time approved by the State of the Operator.

id: CAR-DEF|Extended range operation by twin- engine aeroplane
article_no: Extended range operation by twin- engine aeroplane
title: Extended range operation by twin- engine aeroplane
text: See: Extended diversion time operations

title: Extended twin-engine operation
text: See: Extended diversion time operations.

title: Extended Diversion Time Operations (EDTO)
text: Any operation by an aeroplane with two or more turbine engines where the diversion time to an en-route alternate aerodrome is greater than the threshold time established by the State of the Operator.

title: External equipment (helicopter)
text: Any instrument, mechanism, part, apparatus, appurtenance, or accessory that is attached to or extends from the helicopter exterior but is not used nor is intended to be used for operating or controlling a helicopter in flight and is not part of an airframe or engine.

title: External load
text: A load that is carried, towed or extends, outside the aircraft fuselage.

title: External load attaching means
text: The structural components used to attach an external load to an aircraft, including external-load containers, the backup structure at the attachment points, and any quick-release device used to jettison the external load.

title: Facilitation
text: The efficient management of a necessary control process, with the objective to expediting the clearance of persons or goods and prevent unnecessary operational delays.

title: Factor of safety
text: A design factor used to provide for the possibility of loads greater than those assumed, and for uncertainties in design and fabrication.

title: Fan marker beacon
text: A type of radio beacon, the emissions of which radiate in a vertical fan-shaped pattern.

title: Fatal injury
text: Any injury, which results in death within thirty days of the accident.

title: Farad
text: The capacitance of a capacitor between the plates of which there appears a difference of potential of 1 volt when it is charged by a quantity of electricity equal to 1 coulomb.

title: Fatigue
text: A physiological state of reduced mental or physical performance capability resulting from sleep loss or extended wakefulness, circadian phase, or workload (mental and/or physical activity) that can impair a crew member’s alertness and ability to safely operate an aircraft or impair the ability of any other person to perform safety-related duties. For other than crewmember area, the crewmember may be replaced with safety related personnel.

title: Fatigue Applicable 5 November 2020
text: A physiological state of reduced mental or physical performance capability resulting from sleep loss, extended wakefulness, circadian phase, and/or workload (mental and/or physical activity) that can impair a person’s alertness and ability to perform safety-related operational duties.

id: CAR-DEF|Fatigue Risk Management System (FRMS). Applicable 5 November 2020
article_no: Fatigue Risk Management System (FRMS). Applicable 5 November 2020
title: Fatigue Risk Management System (FRMS). Applicable 5 November 2020
text: A data-driven means of continuously monitoring and managing fatigue- related safety risks, based upon scientific principles and knowledge as well as operational experience that aims to ensure relevant personnel AN6/III, are performing at adequate levels of alertness.

title: Feature
text: Abstraction of real world phenomena (ISO 19101*). *ISO Standard 19101, Geographic information; Reference model.

title: Feature attribute
text: Characteristic of a feature (ISO 19101*). *ISO Standard 19101, Geographic information; Reference model. Note.— A feature attribute has a name, a data type and a value domain associated with it.

title: Feature operation
text: Operation that every instance of a feature type may perform (ISO 19110*). *ISO Standard 19110, Geographic information; Feature cataloguing schema. Note.— An operation upon the feature type dam is to raise the dam. The result of this operation is to raise the level of water in the reservoir.

title: Feature relationship
text: Relationship that links instances of one feature type with instances of the same or a different feature type (ISO 19101*). *ISO Standard 19101, Geographic information; Reference model.

title: Feature type
text: Class of real world phenomena with common properties (ISO 19110*). *ISO Standard 19110, Geographic information; Feature cataloguing schema. Note.— In a feature catalogue, the basic level of classification is the feature type

title: Feedstock
text: A type of unprocessed raw material used for the production of aviation fuel.

title: Feet
text: See: Foot.

title: Filed flight Plan (FPL)
text: The flight plan as filed with an ATS unit by the pilot or a designated representative, without any subsequent changes.

title: Final approach (FNA)
text: That part of an instrument approach procedure which commences at the specified final approach fix or point, or where such a fix or point is not specified, a) at the end of the last procedure turn, base turn or inbound turn of a racetrack procedure, if specified; or b) at the point of interception of the last track specified in the approach procedure; and ends at a point in the vicinity of an aerodrome from which: 1) a landing can be made; or 2) a missed approach procedure is initiated.

title: Final Approach and Take-Off area (FATO)
text: A defined area over which the final phase of the approach manoeuvre to hover or landing is completed and from which the take-off manoeuvre is commenced. Where the FATO is to be used by performance Class 1 helicopters operating in An6/III, performance Class 1, the defined area includes the rejected take-off area available.

title: Final Approach Fix or point (FAF)
text: That fix or point of an instrument approach procedure where the final approach segment commences.

title: Final Approach Segment (FAS)
text: That segment of an instrument approach procedure in which alignment and descent for landing are accomplished. OPS/I,

title: Final take-off speed
text: The speed of the aeroplane that exists at the end of the take-off path in the en- route configuration with one engine inoperative.

title: Fire resistant
text: The capability to withstand the application of heat by a flame for a period of 5 minutes. NOTE: The characteristics of an acceptable flame can be found in ISO 2685.

title: Fireproof
text: Fireproof. The capability to withstand the application of heat by a flame for a period of 15 minutes. Note.— The characteristics of an acceptable flame can be found in ISO 2685.

title: Fireproof material
text: A material capable of withstanding heat as well as or better than steel when the dimensions in both cases are appropriate for the specific purpose.

title: First aid oxygen
text: The additional oxygen provided for the use of passengers, who do not satisfactorily recover following subjection to excessive cabin altitudes, during which they had been provided with supplemental oxygen.

title: Fixed light
text: A light having constant luminous intensity when observed from a fixed point.

title: Fixed message sign
text: A sign presenting only one message.

title: Fixed Pitch Propeller
text: A propeller, the pitch of which cannot be changed, except by processes constituting a workshop operation.

title: Flame resistant
text: Not susceptible to combustion to the point of propagating a flame, beyond safe limits, after the ignition source is removed.

title: Flammable
text: With respect to a fluid or gas, means susceptible to igniting readily or exploding.

title: Flap extended speed
text: The highest speed permissible with wing-flaps in a prescribed extended position.

title: Flash resistant
text: Not susceptible to burning violently when ignited.

title: Flight crew member
text: A licensed crew member charged with duties essential to the operation of an aircraft during a flight duty period. AN6/III, AN11,

extra.icao_source: AN1, AN2, AN3, AN6/I, AN6/II, AN9, AN18, ATM

title: Flight Data Analysis (FDA)
text: A process of analysing recorded flight data in order to improve the safety of flight operations.

title: Flight Data Monitoring (FDM)
text: See: Flight Data Analysis.

title: Flight documentation
text: Written or printed documents, including charts or forms, containing meteorological information for a flight.

title: Flight duty period
text: A period which commences when an Operating Crew Member is required to COMMISSION report for duty that includes a flight or a series of flights and which finishes REGULATION when the aeroplane finally comes to rest at the end of the last flight on which he/she is an operating Crew Member. air

title: Flight duty period
text: A period which commences when a flight or cabin crew member is required to report for duty that includes a flight or a series of flights and which finishes when the aircraft finally comes to rest and the engines are shut down at the end of the last flight on which he/she is a crew member.

title: Flight Information Centre (FIC)
text: A unit established to provide flight information service and alerting service.

title: Flight Information Region (FIR)
text: An airspace of defined dimensions within which flight information service and alerting service are provided.

title: Flight Information Service (FIS)
text: A service provided for the purpose of giving advice and information useful for the safe and efficient conduct of flights.

extra.icao_source: AN2, AN3, AN4, AN11, ATM AN2, AN10/III, AN11, ATM

title: Flight Level (FL)
text: A surface of constant atmospheric pressure which is related to a specific pressure datum, 1 013.2 hectopascals (hpa), and is separated from other such surfaces by specific pressure intervals. Note 1.— A pressure type altimeter calibrated in accordance with the Standard Atmosphere: AN4, a) when set to a QNH altimeter setting, will indicate altitude; b) when set to a QFE altimeter setting, will indicate height above the QFE reference datum; c) when set to a pressure of 1 013.2 hPa, may be used to indicate flight levels. Note 2.— The terms “height” and “altitude”, used in Note 1 above, indicate altimetric rather than geometric heights and altitudes.

extra.icao_source: AN2, AN3, AN10/II, AN11, 9388, ATM, OPS/II

title: Flight manual
text: A manual, associated with the certificate of airworthiness, containing limitations within which the aircraft is to be considered airworthy, and instructions and information necessary to the flight crew members for the safe operation of the aircraft.

title: Flight operations officer/flight dispatcher
text: A person designated by the operator to engage in the control and supervision of flight operations, whether licensed or not, suitably qualified in accordance with Annex 1, who supports, briefs, and/or assists the pilot in command in the safe conduct of the flight.

title: Flight Plan (PLN)
text: Specified information provided to air traffic services units, relative to an intended flight or portion of a flight of an aircraft.

extra.icao_source: AN1, AN2, AN6/I, AN6/II, AN6/III, AN11, AN16/IV, ATM

title: Flight procedures trainer
text: See: Flight simulation training device.

id: CAR-DEF|Flight procedures trainer (Apparatus) Applicable until 2 November 2022.
article_no: Flight procedures trainer (Apparatus) Applicable until 2 November 2022.
title: Flight procedures trainer (Apparatus) Applicable until 2 November 2022.
text: Which provides a realistic flight deck environment, and which simulates instrument responses, simple control functions of mechanical, electrical, electronic, etc. Aircraft systems, and the performance and flight characteristics of aircraft of a particular class.

title: Flight recorder
text: Any type of recorder installed in the aircraft for the purpose of complementing accident/incident investigation. AN6/III,

title: Flight safety documents system
text: A set of inter-related documentation established by the operator, compiling and organising information necessary for flight and ground operations, and comprising, as a minimum, the operations manual and the operators’ CAME.

title: Flight sector
text: A flight or one of a series of flights which commences at a parking place of the aircraft and terminates at a parking place of the aircraft.

id: CAR-DEF|Flight simulation training device Applicable until 2 November 2022.
article_no: Flight simulation training device Applicable until 2 November 2022.
title: Flight simulation training device Applicable until 2 November 2022.
text: Any one of the following three types of apparatus in which flight conditions are simulated on the ground: A flight simulator, which provides an accurate representation of the flight deck of a particular aircraft type to the extent that the mechanical, electrical, electronic, etc. aircraft systems control functions, the normal environment of flight crew members, and the performance and flight characteristics of that type of aircraft are realistically simulated; AN6/I,AN6/II, A flight procedures trainer, which provides a realistic flight deck environment, and which simulates instrument responses, simple control functions of mechanical, electrical, electronic, etc. aircraft systems, and the performance and flight characteristics of aircraft of a particular class; A basic instrument flight trainer, which is equipped with appropriate instruments, and which simulates the flight deck environment of an aircraft in f light in instrument flight conditions.

id: CAR-DEF|Flight simulation training device Applicable as of 3
article_no: Flight simulation training device Applicable as of 3
title: Flight simulation training device Applicable as of 3
text: Any one of the following three types of apparatus in which flight conditions are simulated on the ground: A flight simulator, which provides an accurate representation of the flight deck

title: November 2022.
text: of a particular aircraft type or an accurate representation of the remotely piloted aircraft system (RPAS) to the extent that the mechanical, electrical, electronic, etc. aircraft systems control functions, the normal environment of flight crew members, and the performance and flight characteristics of that type of aircraft are realistically simulated; A flight procedures trainer, which provides a realistic flight deck environment or realistic RPAS environment, and which simulates instrument responses, simple control functions of mechanical, electrical, electronic, etc. aircraft systems, and the performance and flight characteristics of aircraft of a particular class;

title: Flight simulator
text: A basic instrument flight trainer, which is equipped with appropriate instruments, and which simulates the flight deck environment of an aircraft in flight or the RPAS environment in instrument flight conditions. See Flight simulation training device

title: Flight simulator Applicable until 2 November 2022.
text: [Apparatus] which provides an accurate representation of the flight deck of a particular aircraft type to the extent that the mechanical, electrical, electronic, etc. Aircraft systems control functions, the normal environment of flight crew members, and the performance and flight characteristics of that type of aircraft are realistically simulated.

id: CAR-DEF|Flight simulator Applicable as of 3 November 2022
article_no: Flight simulator Applicable as of 3 November 2022
title: Flight simulator Applicable as of 3 November 2022
text: [Apparatus] which provides an accurate representation of the flight deck of a particular aircraft type or an accurate representation of the remotely piloted aircraft system (RPAS) to the extent that the mechanical, electrical, electronic, etc. aircraft systems control functions, the normal environment of flight crew members, and the performance and flight characteristics of that type of aircraft are realistically simulated

title: Flight status
text: An indication of whether a given aircraft requires special handling by air traffic services units or not.

title: Flight time – aeroplanes
text: The total time from the moment an aeroplane first moves for the purpose of taking off until the moment it finally comes to rest at the end of the flight. NOTE: Flight time as here defined is synonymous with the term “block to block” time or “chock to chock” time in general usage which is measured from the time an aeroplane first moves for the purpose of taking off until it finally stops at the end of the flight.

title: Flight time – helicopters
text: The total time from the moment a helicopter’s rotor blades start turning until the moment the helicopter finally comes to rest at the end of the flight, and the rotor blades are stopped.

id: CAR-DEF|Flight time — remotely piloted aircraft systems
article_no: Flight time — remotely piloted aircraft systems
title: Flight time — remotely piloted aircraft systems
text: The total time from the moment a command and control (C2) link is established between the remote pilot station (RPS) and the remotely piloted aircraft (RPA) for the purpose of taking off or from the moment the remote pilot receives control following a handover until the moment the remote pilot completes a handover or the C2 link between the RPS and the RPA is terminated at the end of the flight.

title: Flight track
text: See: Track.

title: Flight visibility
text: The visibility forward from the cockpit of an aircraft in flight.

title: Flight Watch System
text: A system described in the operator's Operations Manual for the monitoring of an aircraft during flight time.

title: Flow control
text: Measures designed to adjust the flow of traffic into a given airspace, along a given route, or bound for a given aerodrome, so as to ensure the most effective utilization of the airspace.

title: Fly-by waypoint
text: A waypoint which requires turn anticipation to allow tangential interception of the next segment of a route or procedure.

title: Flyover waypoint
text: A waypoint at which a turn is initiated in order to join the next segment of a route or procedure.

extra.icao_source: AN4, AN11, ATM, OPS/I, OPS/II AN4, AN11, ATM, OPS/I, OPS/II

title: Foot/ feet (ft)
text: The length equal to 0.3048 metre exactly.

title: Forecast (FCST)
text: A statement of expected meteorological conditions for a specified time or period, and for a specified area or portion of airspace.

title: Forecast chart
text: See: Prognostic chart.

title: Foreign aircraft
text: Civil aircraft registered in a foreign state.

title: Foreign object debris (FOD)
text: An inanimate object within the movement area which has no operational or aeronautical function and which has the potential to be a hazard to aircraft operations.

title: Force Majeure
text: A statement included in contracts to remove liability for natural and unavoidable catastrophes that interrupt the expected course of events and restrict recipients from fulfilling obligations.

title: Forward error correction (FEC)
text: The process of adding redundant information to the transmitted signal in a manner which allows correction, at the receiver, of errors incurred in the transmission.

title: Frangible object
text: An object of low mass designed to break, distort or yield on impact so as to present the minimum hazard to aircraft.

title: Free text message element
text: Part of a message that does not conform to any standard message element in the PANS-ATM (Doc 4444).

title: Free zone
text: A part of the territory of a Contracting State where any goods introduced are generally regarded, insofar as import duties and taxes are concerned, as being outside the customs territory.

title: Freight
text: See: Cargo/ Freight. A continuous portion of the frequency spectrum appropriate for a transmission utilizing a specified class of emission.

title: Frequency channel
text: Note.— The classification of emissions and information relevant to the portion of the frequency spectrum appropriate for a given type of transmission (bandwidths) are specified in the ITU Radio Regulations, Article S2 and Appendix S1.

title: Fuel uplift
text: Measurement of fuel provided by the fuel supplier, as documented in the fuel delivery notes or invoices for each flight (in litre).

title: Fully automatic relay installation
text: A teletypewriter installation where interpretation of the relaying responsibility in respect of an incoming message and the resultant setting-up of the connections required to effect the appropriate retransmissions is carried out automatically, as well as all other normal operations of relay, thus obviating the need for operator intervention, except for supervisory purposes.

title: Gain-to-noise temperature ratio
text: The ratio, usually expressed in dB/K, of the antenna gain to the noise at the receiver output of the antenna subsystem. The noise is expressed as the temperature that a 1 ohm resistor must be raised to produce the same noise power density.

title: GAMET area forecast
text: An area forecast in abbreviated plain language for low-level flights for a flight information region or sub-area thereof, prepared by the meteorological office designated by the meteorological authority concerned and exchanged with meteorological offices in adjacent flight information regions, as agreed between the meteorological authorities concerned.

title: GBAS Landing System (GLS)
text: An approach landing system using ground based augmented global navigation satellite system (GNSS/GBAS) information to provide guidance to the aircraft based on its lateral and vertical GNSS position. It uses geometric altitude reference for its final approach slope.

title: GCAA
text: General Civil Aviation Authority or any of its departments to which supervision and development of civil aviation affairs is assigned.

title: General aviation operation
text: An aircraft operation other than a commercial air transport operation or an aerial work operation. AN6/III,

title: Geodesic distance
text: The shortest distance between any two points on a mathematically defined ellipsoidal surface.

title: Geodetic datum
text: A minimum set of parameters required to define location and orientation of the local reference system with respect to the global reference system/frame.

title: Geoid
text: The equipotential surface in the gravity field of the Earth, which coincides with the undisturbed mean sea level (MSL) extended continuously through the AN4, continents. Note.— The geoid is irregular in shape because of local gravitational AN15, disturbances (wind tides, salinity, current, etc.) and the direction of gravity is perpendicular to the geoid at every point.

title: Geoid Undulation (GUND)
text: The distance of the geoid above (positive) or below (negative) the mathematical reference ellipsoid. Note.— In respect to the World Geodetic System — 1984 (WGS-84) defined ellipsoid, the difference between the WGS-84 ellipsoidal height and orthometric height represents WGS-84 geoid undulation.

title: Glide Path (GP)
text: A descent profile determined for vertical guidance during a final approach.

title: Glider (GLD)
text: See: Sailplane. A non-power-driven heavier-than-air aircraft, deriving its lift in flight chiefly from aerodynamic reactions on surfaces which remain fixed under given conditions of flight.

title: Glider flight time
text: The total time occupied in flight, whether being towed or not, from the moment the glider first moves for the purpose of taking off until the moment it comes to rest at the end of the flight.

title: Go-around power or thrust setting
text: The maximum allowable in-flight power or thrust setting identified in the performance data.

title: Gravity-related height
text: See: Elevation.

title: Gray (Gy)
text: The energy imparted by ionizing radiation to a mass of matter corresponding to 1 joule per kilogram.

title: Great Circle Distance
text: The shortest distance, rounded to the nearest kilometre, between the origin and the destination aerodromes, measured over the earth’s surface modelled according to the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS84). Note.— Latitude and longitude coordinates of aerodromes can be obtained from

extra.icao_source: AN16/IV the ICAO Location Indicators database.

title: Gregorian calendar
text: Calendar in general use; first introduced in 1582 to define a year that more closely approximates the tropical year than the Julian calendar (ISO 19108*). *ISO Standard 19108, Geographic information; Temporal schema Note.— In the Gregorian calendar, common years have 365 days and leap years 366 days divided into twelve sequential months.

id: CAR-DEF|Grid point data in digital form
article_no: Grid point data in digital form
title: Grid point data in digital form
text: Computer processed meteorological data for a set of regularly spaced points on a chart, for transmission from a meteorological computer to another computer in a code form suitable for automated use. Note.— In most cases, such data are transmitted on medium- or high-speed telecommunications channels.

title: Ground earth station (GES)
text: An earth station in the fixed satellite service, or, in some cases, in the aeronautical mobile-satellite service, located at a specified fixed point on land to provide a feeder link for the aeronautical mobilesatellite service. Note.— This definition is used in the ITU’s Radio Regulations under the term “aeronautical earth station”. The definition herein as “GES” for use in the SARPs is to clearly distinguish it from an aircraft earth station (AES), which is a mobile station on an aircraft.

title: Gross negligence
text: Means a manifest and wilful violation of the duty of care directly causing foreseeable damage to a person or to a property, or which seriously lowers the level of aviation safety.

title: Ground effect
text: A condition of improved performance (lift) due to the interference of the surface with the airflow pattern of the rotor system when a helicopter or other VTOL aircraft is operating near the ground.

title: Ground equipment
text: Articles of a specialized nature for use in the maintenance, repair and servicing of an aircraft on the ground, including testing equipment and cargo-and passenger-handling equipment.

title: Ground handling
text: Services necessary for an aircraft’s arrival at, and departure from, an airport, other than air traffic services.

title: Ground track
text: See: Track.

title: Ground visibility
text: The visibility at an aerodrome, as reported by an accredited observer or by automatic systems.

title: Grounding
text: The formal prohibition of an aircraft to take-off and the taking of such steps as are necessary to detain it.

title: Ground-to-air communication
text: One-way communication from stations or locations on the surface of the earth AN10/II, to aircraft.

title: Gyroplane
text: A heavier-than-air aircraft supported in flight by the reactions of the air on one or more rotors which rotate freely on substantially vertical axes.

title: Guarantee contract
text: Means a contract entered into by a person as guarantor.

title: Handover
text: The act of passing piloting control from one remote pilot station to another

title: Hazard
text: A condition or an object with the potential to cause or contribute to an aircraft incident or accident.

title: Hazard Beacon (HBN)
text: An aeronautical beacon used to designate a danger to air navigation.

title: Heading (HDG)
text: The direction in which the longitudinal axis of an aircraft is pointed, usually expressed in degrees from North (true, magnetic, compass or grid). OPS/I,

title: Head-Up Display (HUD)
text: A display system which presents flight information to the pilot's forward external field of view and which does not significantly restrict the external view.

title: Head-Up Display (HUD)
text: A display system that presents flight information into the pilot’s forward external field of view.

title: Head-Up Guidance Landing System (HUDLS)
text: The total airborne system that provides head-up guidance to the pilot during the approach and landing and/or missed approach procedure. It includes all sensors, computers, power supplies, indications and controls.

title: Heavier-than-air aircraft
text: Any aircraft deriving its lift in flight chiefly from aerodynamic forces.

title: Height (HGT)
text: The vertical distance of a level, a point, or an object considered as a point, measured from a specified datum. AN11,

extra.icao_source: AN2, AN3, AN4, AN6/I, AN10/I, AN10/II, AN15, ATM, OPS/I, OPS/II AN6/III, AN16/I, AN19, AN7

title: Helicopter (HEL)
text: A heavier-than-air aircraft supported in flight chiefly by the reactions of the air AN8, on one or more power-driven rotors on substantially vertical axes.

title: Helicopter
text: Heavier-than-air machines (other than those used in military, customs or police services) supported in flight chiefly by the reactions of the air on one or more power-driven rotors on substantially vertical axes and which are type certified by the competent aviation authority to transport: a) At least five (5) persons including crew; or b) Goods in excess of 450 kilograms, together with all installed, incorporated or attached accessories, parts and equipment (including rotors), and all data, manuals and records relating thereto.

title: Helicopter air taxiway
text: A defined path on the surface established for the air taxiing of helicopters.

title: Helicopter clearway
text: A defined area on the ground or water under the control of the appropriate Authority, selected and/or prepared as a suitable area over which a performance Class 1 helicopter may accelerate and achieve a specific height.

title: Helicopter ground taxiway
